title: Computing query results causes attributes to be dropped
description:
Let's consider a simple example

```r
sc <- sparklyr::spark_connect(master = "local")
mtcars_spark <- dplyr::copy_to(dest = sc, df = mtcars)

blah <- dplyr::select(mtcars_spark, mpg)                                                                                                                          
attr(blah, "testAttr") <- "hello"                                                                                                                                 
attributes(blah)                                                                                                                                                  
# $names
# [1] "src" "ops"
# $class
# [1] "tbl_spark" "tbl_sql"   "tbl_lazy"  "tbl"      
# $testAttr
# [1] "hello"

blah <- dplyr::compute(blah)                                                                                                                                      
attributes(blah)                                                                                                                                                  
# $names
# [1] "src" "ops"
# $class
# [1] "tbl_spark" "tbl_sql"   "tbl_lazy"  "tbl"
```

When using `dplyr::compute()` on a `tbl_spark` object, for example, it will dispatch to `dbplyr:::compute.tbl_spark()`. I feel like this should maybe have some similar method to `dplyr::dplyr_reconstruct()` to ensure that attributes are not dropped. 

This issue is a copy-pasta of https://github.com/tidyverse/dbplyr/issues/618 which was closed.

title: Consider adding repositories setting to dependencies for extensions
description: Currently, not every spark package is on Central, e.g. https://github.com/tensorflow/ecosystem/issues/29#issuecomment-386852952. The ideal scenario is for upstream dependencies to publish artifacts there, but as a fallback we could consider letting sparklyr extension authors specify resolvers.

title: Broadcast variable support in `spark_apply()`
description: Currently, `spark_apply()`'s `context` parameter distributed additional data by creating an RDD initialized with the specific context. However, if multiple calls to `spark_apply()` are chained, this context will have to be re-transmitted each time. Broadcast variables would make this more efficient. This could be implemented through a new `broadcast` parameter.

out_bucket <- 'gfi-mirror-analysis' # save the results to a S3 bucket called 'gfi-mirror-analysis'
oplog <- 'mirror_match.log' # progress report file
opcounter <- 'mirror_match.csv'
dinfo <- 'bulk_download.log' # file of the information of the downloaded data
keycache <- read.csv('~/vars/accesscodes.csv', header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) # the database of our credentials

#===================================================================================================================================#

ec2env(keycache,usr)
options(stringsAsFactors= FALSE)
log_head <- 'Time\tZone\tYear\tMark\tStatus\n'
if(!file.exists('/efs/logs'))system('sudo mkdir -m777 /efs/logs')
oplog <- paste('/efs/logs/', oplog, sep = '')
config <- spark_config()
config$sparklyr.apply.env.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID <- Sys.getenv('AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID')
config$sparklyr.apply.env.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY <- Sys.getenv('AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY')
config$sparklyr.apply.env.AWS_DEFAULT_REGION <- Sys.getenv('AWS_DEFAULT_REGION')
config$sparklyr.apply.env.log_head <- log_head
config$sparklyr.apply.env.out_bucket <- out_bucket
config$sparklyr.apply.env.oplog <- oplog

sc <- spark_connect(master="local", config = config)
logg <- function(x)mklog(x, path = oplog)
cat(log_head, file = oplog, append = FALSE)
opcounter <- file.path('data', opcounter)
dinfo <- file.path('logs', dinfo); dinfo <- read.delim(dinfo)

dinfo <- unique(dinfo); n_d <- nrow(dinfo)
stopifnot(n_d > 0 & !any(duplicated(dinfo$Year)))

dist_codes <- function(in_df){
  pkgs <- c('aws.s3', 'stats', 'scripting', 'data.table')
  for(i in pkgs)library(i, character.only = T)
  remotes::install_github("sherrisherry/DC-Trees-App", subdir="pkg"); library(pkg)
  #===================================================================================================================================#
  max_try <- 10 # the maximum number of attempts for a failed process
  in_bucket <- 'gfi-comtrade' # read in raw data from this bucket
  sup_bucket <- 'gfi-supplemental' # supplemental files
  tag <- "Comtrade"
  cols_UN <- rep('NULL', 15)
  names(cols_UN) <- c("classification","year","period","perioddesc","aggregatelevel","isleafcode","tradeflowcode",
                      "reportercode","partnercode", "commoditycode","qtyunitcode","qty","netweightkg","tradevalues","flag")
  incol <- c("tradeflowcode","classification","reportercode","partnercode","commoditycode", "tradevalues", "qtyunitcode", "qty", "netweightkg")
  names(incol) <- c("tf","hs","i","j","k","v","q_code","q","q_kg")
  cols_UN[incol] <- c("integer","character","integer","integer","character","numeric","integer","numeric","numeric")
  cols_swiss <- c("character","integer","character","integer",rep("numeric",2))
  names(cols_swiss) <- c('mx','j','k','t','v','q_kg')
  cols_hk <- c(rep('integer', 2), 'character', 'numeric')
  names(cols_hk) <- c("origin_un","consig_un","k","vrx_un")
  # use "character" for k or codes like '9999AA' messes up
  tfn <- c('M','rM','X','rX')
  names(tfn) <- c('1','4','2','3')
  out_names <- c('M_matched', 'X_matched', 'M_orphaned', 'M_lost')
  names(out_names) <- c('M.FALSE', 'X.FALSE', 'M.TRUE', 'X.TRUE') # M_lost == X_orphan
  #===================================================================================================================================#
  out_bucket <- Sys.getenv('out_bucket')
  oplog <- Sys.getenv('oplog')
  logg <- function(x)mklog(x, path = oplog)
  options(stringsAsFactors= FALSE)
  cat(Sys.getenv('log_head'), file = oplog, append = FALSE)
  # Prepare for SWISS module
  # Data M_swiss and X_swiss compiled by Joe Spanjers from Swiss source data
  ecycle(swiss <- s3read_using(FUN = function(x)fread(x, header=T, na.strings="", colClasses = cols_swiss), 
                               object = "Swiss_mx_71-72.csv", bucket = sup_bucket),
         {tmp <- paste('0000', '!', 'loading Swiss failed', sep = '\t'); logg(tmp); stop(tmp)},
         max_try)
  # # keep only records for commodity 710812 which comprises 98% of Swiss trade in non-monetary gold
  #     (NB, monetary gold trade flows should not be included in UN-Comtrade dataset for any country)
  swiss <- subset(swiss,swiss$k=='710812'); swiss <- split(swiss, swiss$mx)
  opcounter <- list() # setup counter
  # Loop by date
  print(in_df)
  for (year in in_df$Year){
    counter <- c(year = year)
    # Start RAW module
    ecycle(save_object(object = paste(year, '.csv.bz2', sep = ''), bucket = in_bucket, file = 'tmp/tmp.csv.bz2', overwrite = TRUE),
           {logg(paste(year, '!', 'retrieving file failed', sep = '\t')); next}, max_try)
    ecycle(rdata <- fread(cmd = "bzip2 -dkc ./tmp/tmp.csv.bz2", header=T, colClasses = cols_UN),
           {logg(paste(year, '!', 'loading file failed', sep = '\t')); next}, max_try,
           cond = is.data.table(rdata))
    if(!setequal(colnames(rdata), incol)){
      logg(paste(year, '!', 'colnames mismatching', sep = '\t'))
      next
    }
    logg(paste(year, ':', 'opened', sep = '\t'))
    if(nrow(rdata) != in_df$Status[in_df$Year==year]){logg(paste(year, '#', nrow(rdata), sep = '\t'))}
    # avoid reordering data table because of speed
    tmp <- colnames(rdata)
    colnames(rdata)[match(incol, tmp)] <- names(incol)
    rdata <- na.omit(rdata, cols=c("hs","i","j","k","v"))
    setkeyv(rdata, c('i', 'j', 'k'))
    logg(paste(year, ':', 'preprocessed', sep = '\t'))
    rdata<- split(rdata, rdata$tf)
    names(rdata) <- tfn[match(names(rdata),names(tfn))]
    rdata <- lapply(rdata, function(x){cols <- colnames(x); nm <- c("v","q_code","q","q_kg"); lsn <- tfn[as.character(x$tf[1])]
    colnames(x)[match(nm, cols)] <- paste(nm, lsn, sep = '_'); x$tf <- NULL
    return(x)})
    tmp <- sapply(rdata, nrow); names(tmp) <- paste('raw', names(tmp), sep = '_')
    counter <- append(counter, tmp); print(counter)
    logg(paste(year, '#', paste(paste(names(tmp), tmp, sep = ':'), collapse = ','), sep = '\t'))
    #   End RAW module
    
    #   Implement TREAT module 
    rdata <- lapply(rdata, function(x)unct_treat(x, year))
    tmp <- sapply(rdata, nrow); names(tmp) <- paste('treat', names(tmp), sep = '_')
    counter <- append(counter, tmp); print(counter)
    logg(paste(year, '#', paste(paste(names(tmp), tmp, sep = ':'), collapse = ','), sep = '\t'))
    
    #   End TREAT module
    
    #   Implement SWISS module
    rdata$M  <- unct_swiss(rdata$M,swiss$m,year); rdata$X  <- unct_swiss(rdata$X,swiss$x,year)
    tmp <- sapply(rdata, nrow); names(tmp) <- paste('swiss', names(tmp), sep = '_')
    counter <- append(counter, tmp); print(counter)
    logg(paste(year, '#', paste(paste(names(tmp), tmp, sep = ':'), collapse = ','), sep = '\t'))
    # End SWISS module
    
    #   Start PAIR module
    # Pair M
    tmp <- colnames(rdata$M); colnames(rdata$M)[match('hs', tmp)] <- c('hs_rpt')
    tmp <- colnames(rdata$X); colnames(rdata$X)[match(c('hs', 'i', 'j'), tmp)] <- c('hs_ptn', 'j', 'i')
    tmp <- colnames(rdata$rX); colnames(rdata$rX)[match(c('i', 'j'), tmp)] <- c('j', 'i')
    mirror <- list()
    mirror$M <- merge(x=rdata$M,y=rdata$X,by = c("i","j","k"), all.x=TRUE)
    mirror$M <- merge(x=mirror$M,y=rdata$rX[, c("i","j","k","v_rX")],by = c("i","j","k"), all.x=TRUE)
    mirror$M <- merge(x=mirror$M,y=rdata$rM[, c("i","j","k","v_rM")],by = c("i","j","k"), all.x=TRUE)
    
    logg(paste(year, ':', 'M-paired', sep = '\t'))
    
    # Pair X
    tmp <- colnames(rdata$X); colnames(rdata$X)[match(c('hs_ptn', 'i', 'j'), tmp)] <- c('hs_rpt', 'j', 'i')
    tmp <- colnames(rdata$M); colnames(rdata$M)[match(c('hs_rpt', 'i', 'j'), tmp)] <- c('hs_ptn', 'j', 'i')
    tmp <- colnames(rdata$rM); colnames(rdata$rM)[match(c('i', 'j'), tmp)] <- c('j', 'i')
    tmp <- colnames(rdata$rX); colnames(rdata$rX)[match(c('i', 'j'), tmp)] <- c('j', 'i')
    mirror$X <- merge(x=rdata$X,y=rdata$M,by = c("i","j","k"), all.x=TRUE)
    mirror$X <- merge(x=mirror$X,y=rdata$rX[, c("i","j","k","v_rX")],by = c("i","j","k"), all.x=TRUE)
    mirror$X <- merge(x=mirror$X,y=rdata$rM[, c("i","j","k","v_rM")],by = c("i","j","k"), all.x=TRUE)
    
    rm(rdata)
    logg(paste(year, ':', 'X-paired', sep = '\t'))
    # end PAIR module
    
    # Start Hong Kong module
    # operate on X-paired and M-paired and then redo the matching etc
    # use normalized hkrx data
    hk <- in_hkrx(year, names(cols_hk), cols_hk, logf = logg, max_try = max_try)
    if(is.null(hk))next
    mirror$M <- unct_hk(mirror$M, hk, year, 'M', logg, max_try, out_bucket); if(is.null(mirror$M))next
    mirror$X <- unct_hk(mirror$X, hk, year, 'X', logg, max_try, out_bucket); if(is.null(mirror$X))next
    # end Hong Kong module
    
    tmp <- sapply(mirror, nrow); names(tmp) <- paste(names(tmp), 'pair', sep = '_')
    counter <- append(counter, tmp); print(counter)
    logg(paste(year, '#', paste(paste(names(tmp), tmp, sep = ':'), collapse = ','), sep = '\t'))
    
    # Start MATCH module
    # Matching M
    mirror$M <- split(mirror$M, is.na(mirror$M$v_X))
    mirror$X <- split(mirror$X, is.na(mirror$X$v_M))
    mirror <- unlist(mirror, recursive = F)
    # mirror$M.FALSE should equal mirror$X.FALSE
    stopifnot(setequal(names(mirror),names(out_names)))
    names(mirror) <- out_names[names(mirror)]
    # renamed mirror to match out_names
    tmp <- sapply(mirror, nrow)
    counter <- append(counter, tmp); print(counter)
    logg(paste(year, '#', paste(paste(names(tmp), tmp, sep = ':'), collapse = ','), sep = '\t'))
    # end MATCH module
    
    # verify matched M==X
    if(counter['M_matched']==counter['X_matched']){
      tmp <- colnames(mirror$X_matched)
      colnames(mirror$X_matched)[match(c("hs_rpt","hs_ptn","i","j"), tmp)] <- c("hs_ptn","hs_rpt","j","i")
      tmp <- duplicated(rbind(mirror$M_matched, mirror$X_matched))
      if(sum(tmp)!=counter['M_matched'])logg(paste(year, '!', 'MX nrow not identical', sep = '\t'))
      else{logg(paste(year, ':', 'identical', sep = '\t')); mirror$X_matched <-NULL}
    }else logg(paste(year, '!', 'MX not identical', sep = '\t'))
    
    # uploading results
    tmp <- paste(tag, year, names(mirror), sep = '-'); tmp <- paste('tmp/', tmp, '.csv.bz2', sep = '')
    names(tmp) <- names(mirror)
    for(i in names(mirror)){
      ecycle(write.csv(mirror[[i]], file = bzfile(tmp[i]), row.names=F, na=""), 
             ecycle(s3write_using(mirror[[i]], FUN = function(x, y)write.csv(x, file=bzfile(y), row.names = F, na=''),
                                  bucket = out_bucket, object = basename(tmp[i])),
                    logg(paste(year, '!', paste('uploading', basename(tmp[i]), 'failed', sep = ' '), sep = '\t')), max_try), 
             max_try,
             ecycle(put_object(tmp[i], basename(tmp[i]), bucket = out_bucket), 
                    logg(paste(year, '!', paste('uploading', basename(tmp[i]), 'failed', sep = ' '), sep = '\t')),
                    max_try,
                    {logg(paste(year, '|', paste('uploaded', basename(tmp[i]), sep = ' '), sep = '\t')); unlink(tmp[i])}))
    }
    rm(mirror)
    print(in_df); print(year)
    opcounter[[as.character(year)]] <- counter; print(opcounter)
  }
  opcounter <- do.call(rbind, opcounter); print(opcounter); print(nrow(opcounter))
  return(opcounter)
}

logg(paste('0000', '|', 'cluster started', sep = '\t'))
tbl_dinfo <- sdf_copy_to(sc, dinfo, repartition = ceiling(n_d/2))
dist_counter <- spark_apply(tbl_dinfo, dist_codes, packages = F, memory = T, name = 'cnt') %>% sdf_collect()
logg(paste('0000', '|', 'cluster ended', sep = '\t'))
write.csv(dist_counter, file = opcounter, row.names = F)
spark_disconnect(sc)

title: Why is "tbl_spark" faster than "SparkDataFrame" ?
description:
I am benchmarking `R` and `Spark` for my particular dataset. I benchmarked random forest ML method on both `R` `dataframe` and `SparkR` `SparkDataFrame`. Long story short, `R` is faster than `SparkR` on small dataset, and `SparkR` is faster than `R` on large dataset. I was happy with this benchmark (as this is a known fact).
Out of curiosity, I ran the same benchmark on `Sparklyr` `tbl_spark` object, and it was faster than both `R` and `SparkR` by 40x and 30x respectively. `Sparklyr` definitely called more number of garbage collectors (~15) than `R` (~4) or `SparkR` (0). And used more memory than `SparkR` (but less than `R`).

Before I go into the specifics of the code and dataset, why is this so? Does `tbl_spark` get loaded into memory? I am asking this because it takes longer to load the same file in `Sparklyr` than in `SparkR` (this might be a different question). 

I am quite confused.

Things to note - 
1. I kept the Spark's configuration same.
2. Same dataset used (`bench::press` and `bench::mark` used for benchmarking over different combination of rows and columns).
3. Random forest parameters were kept the same.
4. Each benchmark was run 5 times, and the median time was compared.

title: spark_read_... fail if a named character is provided as the `name` argument
description:
When reading data using spark_read_..., providing a named character as the `name` argument to the functions will fail.

### Reproducible example

```r
# Attach sparklyr, create dummy csv, connect
library(sparklyr)
objDef <- c(objName = "mtcars", filePath = path.expand("~/mtcars.csv"))
write.csv(mtcars, objDef["filePath"])
sc <- spark_connect("local")

# This does not work
tbl_mtcars <- spark_read_csv(sc, objDef["objName"], objDef["filePath"])

# Error: org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.parser.ParseException:
#   mismatched input '`objName`' expecting {'(', 'SELECT', 'FROM', 'WITH', 'VALUES', 'TABLE', 'INSERT', 'MAP', 'REDUCE'}(line 1, pos 24)
#
# == SQL ==
#   CACHE TABLE `mtcars` AS `objName`
#------------------------^^^

# While this works fine
tbl_mtcars <- spark_read_csv(sc, unname(objDef["objName"]), objDef["filePath"])

# Cleanup
unlink(objDef["filePath"])
spark_disconnect(sc)
```
## Cause analysis

The cause is that the read functions call `spark_partition_register_df` with `memory=TRUE` by defaultwhich will try to send `dbSendQuery(sc, paste("CACHE TABLE", escape(ident(name), con = sc)))`. The issue arises because `dbplyr:::escape.ident()` will use `dbplyr:::names_to_as()` and thus create SQL such as the above `CACHE TABLE `mtcars` AS `objName`` that will cause a ParseExepction.

## Suggested fix

In PR: https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/pull/2175

title: Sanitize table names in copy_to()
description:
Dots in destination table names cause errors.

```r
library(dplyr)
library(sparklyr)

local_tbl <- data_frame(
  x = runif(5)
)
spark_conn <- spark_connect("local")
spark_tbl <- copy_to(spark_conn, local_tbl, "foo.bar")
## Error: org.apache.spark.sql.AnalysisException: 
##    It is not allowed to add database prefix `foo` for the TEMPORARY view name.
spark_tbl <- copy_to(spark_conn, local_tbl, "foo.1")
##  Error: org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.parser.ParseException: 
##    extraneous input '.1' expecting <EOF>(line 1, pos 3)
```

It would be nice if the table names were checked before they were sent to Spark. I'm not sure if the best behavior is to throw a helpful error or to fix the name.

```r
library("sparklyr")

sc <- spark_connect(master = "yarn-client",version = "2.2.0"))

sparkly_prophet <- function(df){

title: Multiple --conf with sparklyr
description:
Hi all,

I'm trying to re-write my Scala code with sparklyr.

With spark-shell, I have

```scala
spark-shell --conf spark.port.maxRetries=100 
--conf spark.sql.session.timeZone=UTC
--conf 'spark.driver.extraJavaOptions=-Duser.timezone=UTC'
--conf 'spark.executor.extraJavaOptions=-Duser.timezone=UTC'
```

but with sparklyr I can't use

```r
conf = spark_config()
conf$`sparklyr.shell.conf` = "spark.port.maxRetries=100"
conf$`sparklyr.shell.conf` = "'spark.executor.extraJavaOptions=-Duser.timezone=UTC'"
conf$`sparklyr.shell.conf` = "'spark.driver.extraJavaOptions=-Duser.timezone=UTC'"
conf$`sparklyr.shell.conf` = "'spark.sql.session.timeZone=UTC'"
spark_connect(master = "yarn-client", spark_home = "/path/to/home/spark", app_name = "test", config = conf)
```

because I only obtain the last one conf 
``` conf$`sparklyr.shell.conf` = "'spark.sql.session.timeZone=UTC'" ```

The workaround I'm using right now is declaring 
``` conf$`sparklyr.shell.conf` ```, 
``` conf$`sparklyr.shell.conf ` ```, 
...
but it seems very inelegant to me.

How can I do this "legally"?

title: no need to run `Rscript ci/.ci.R --coverage` on each pull request
description:
It seems resource-intensive, and also could be time-consuming if other contributors thought they needed to wait for it to finish (they actually don't).
Also, it only needs to be run periodically so running it on all PRs seems a bit wasteful resource-wise.

title: Gateway in localhost:8880 did not respond
description:
Hi there,

I'm running into the well known issue with gateway not responding. In my case it appears to be a port conflict when using the default 8880 port. If I specify a different gateway port in my config, the connection is successful. My question is, how does sparklyr handle conflicting gateway port numbers? My hypothesis is that having a different name for each session seems not enough. I don't know exactly how databricks notebooks works, but I think they have independant R session but with the same GUID.

Maybe it's possible to add another unique identifiant to the name ? (timestamp, hash of the path of the script, ...) Or is there any other workaround (job cluster is not possible due to corporate rules) ?

title: dbExistsTable assumes case sensitivity
description:
If I understand correctly, Spark, by default, is case-insensitive. I was looking at checking for the existence of a table within my Spark context and stumbled across this:

```r
sc <- sparklyr::spark_connect(master = "local")
mtcars_spark <- dplyr::copy_to(dest = sc, df = mtcars)
result <- mtcars_spark %>% dplyr::mutate(bla = 1) %>% sparklyr::sdf_register("testView")

DBI::dbExistsTable(sc, "testView")
# [1] FALSE

DBI::dbListTables(sc)                                                                                                                                              
# [1] "mtcars"   "testview"
```

So I guess there is some kind of comparison going on here. However if I do the same type of check via the Catalog API, this would find it:

```r
ss <- sparklyr::spark_session(sc)
catalog <- sparklyr::invoke(ss, "catalog")

sparklyr::invoke(jobj = catalog, method = "tableExists", "testview")                                                                                               
# [1] TRUE

sparklyr::invoke(jobj = catalog, method = "tableExists", "testView")                                                                                               
# [1] TRUE
```

title: tbl.spark_connection() errors when using a query with join syntax
description:
Let's consider the following data:

```r
sc <- sparklyr::spark_connect(master = "local")
df1 <- data.frame(a = 1, g = 2) %>% dplyr::copy_to(sc, ., "df1")
df2 <- data.frame(b = 1, g = 2) %>% dplyr::copy_to(sc, ., "df2")
```

Let's now do something simple:

```r
tbl(sc, dplyr::sql("select * from df1"))                                                                                                                          
# # Source: spark<select * from df1> [?? x 2]
#       a     g
#   <dbl> <dbl>
# 1     1     2
```

This works! Great! Now let's ramp it up and perform a join:

```r
# Doesn't work:
tbl(sc, dplyr::sql("select df1.a, df2.b, df1.g from df1 left join df2 on df1.g = df2.g"))
# Error in process_tbl_name(from) : 
#   expected input to be <table name> or <schema name>.<table name>

# What about a dplyr verb? Works as expected:
dplyr::left_join(df1, df2, by = "g")                                                                                                                              
# # Source: spark<?> [?? x 3]
#       a     g     b
#   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
# 1     1     2     1

# Let's take a look at the query generated by dbplyr:
dplyr::left_join(df1, df2, by = "g") %>% dbplyr::sql_render()                                                                                                     
# <SQL> SELECT `a`, `LHS`.`g` AS `g`, `b`
# FROM `df1` AS `LHS`
# LEFT JOIN `df2` AS `RHS`
# ON (`LHS`.`g` = `RHS`.`g`)

# Let's try and use this query then
qry <- dplyr::left_join(df1, df2, by = "g") %>% dbplyr::sql_render()  
tbl(sc, qry)
# Error in process_tbl_name(from) : 
#   expected input to be <table name> or <schema name>.<table name>
```

After upgrading all of our packages to the latest versions in the tidyverse this became a problem for us because we have a lot of SQL queries which we execute using `tbl(sc, .)`. Let's look into this some more. When we pass `qry` to `process_tbl_name(from = qry)` (the offending function here) the `components` object is

```
[1] "SELECT `a`, `LHS`"
[2] "`g` AS `g`, `b`\nFROM `df1` AS `LHS`\nLEFT JOIN `df2` AS `RHS`\nON (`LHS`"
[3] "`g` = `RHS`"
[4] "`g`)\n"
```

As expected, it has split on the periods. So the `num_components` is `4` which will always fail based on the current implementation of `process_tbl_name()`. Our current work around is to redefine `tbl.spark_connection()` to remove this function:

```r
tbl.spark_connection <- function(src, from, ...) { 
  src <- dbplyr::src_sql("spark", src) 
  dbplyr::tbl_sql("spark", src = src, from = from, ...) 
}
```

And then all is well.

```r
tbl(sc, dplyr::sql("select df1.a, df2.b, df1.g from df1 left join df2 on df1.g = df2.g"))
# # Source: spark<select df1.a, df2.b, df1.g from df1 left join df2 on df1.g = df2.g> [?? x 3]
#       a     b     g
#   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
# 1     1     1     2
```

EDIT: It would also seem as the `sparklyr::sdf_sql()` works quite well.

title: how to get table name from tbl_spark object?
description:
# Reporting an Issue with sparklyr

I wrote a function that receives a tbl_spark object, uses dbplyr::remote_name to get the name of the table, and creates an SQL queries.   However, sometimes this fails because dbplyr::remote_name returns NULL for tbl_spark objects that are not evaluated yet.

It is frustrating that the class of a tbl_spark remains the same, whether or not it is actually representing a table that exists or what that will be created in the future.

---

Here's my function, which does work as long as the tbl_spark is not waiting lazy evaluation. This is part of a "translation" between IBM DB2 and Spark formats.  The function looks at a given column to find the max and min character lengths. I'm using `invoke` to run my query.  My usage of `dbplyr::remote_name` is causing this to fail with some tbl_spark.

```
# dat is a tbl_spark
str2db <- function(sc, dat, colname, method = "query"){
    ss <- spark_session(sc)
    table_name <- as.character(dbplyr::remote_name(dat))

    buildaselect <- function(x){
        paste(paste0("MAX(LENGTH(", colname, ")) as ", "MAX"), ",",
              paste0("MIN(LENGTH(", colname, ")) as ", "MIN"))
    }
    
    buildquery <- function(table_name, colname){
        paste0("SELECT ", buildaselect(colname), " \n ",
               " FROM ", table_name, " WHERE ", colname, " IS NOT NULL")
    }
    qu <- buildquery(table_name, colname)
    res <- invoke(ss, "sql", qu)
    xmaxmin <- as.data.frame(sdf_collect(res))
    xmax <- xmaxmin[1, "MAX"]
    xmin <- xmaxmin[1, "MIN"]
    if (zapsmall(xmax - xmin) == 0L){
        ret <- paste0("CHAR(", xmax, ")")
    } else if (xmax < 32704) {
        ret <- paste0("VARCHAR(", xmax, ")")
    } else {
        ret <- paste0("CLOB(", xmax, ")")
    }
    ret
}
```


I'm doing this in a cluster that is air-gapped, cannot copy/paste in or out.  But can type, so here it goes:
```r
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)
library(dbplyr)
library(RJDBC)

kernels <- load_spark_kernels()
sc <- spark_connect(kernels[11])

q <- "SELECT * FROM SCH.TESTDATA"

df <- spark_read_jdbc(sc = sc,
                                    name = "fred",
                                    options = list( url = ...,
                                                           driver = ...,,   user = ..., password = ...., query = q)),
                                    memory = FALSE, repartition = 10L)

sdf_num_partitions(df)

# 10

dbplyr::remote_name(df)

# <IDENT> fred

## With that value "fred", I'm able to write Spark SQL queries, the function above works.

## However, if the tbl_spark has any joins or selects, then the call remote_name() returns null 
## and the query fails.

df2 <- df %>% rename("newname" = "oldname")

dbplyr::remote_name(df2)
# NULL
```

The dbplyr documentation says NULL happens when `df2` is a query, and not an evaluated tbl_spark.

What to do?  Can I work around this?

Because this is on an air-gapped system that I do not control, I'm restricted to older versions of packages.

sparklyr  1.0.2
dbplyr 1.4.4
dplyr 1.0.2
RJDBC 0.2-8
rJava 0.9-11

If the age of the packages is the main problem, just let me know to put me out of my misery.

title: All Applications Return Exit Code 1
description:
All sparklyr apps submitted via cli using batch mode are returning exit code 1 regardless of completing successfully. I have encountered this issue on both EMR 6 and Kubernetes (EKS). This includes test jobs (modified from the handy [benchmarks](https://github.com/yitao-li/sparklyr-pyspark-benchmarks/tree/master/sparklyr_spark_apply_benchmark) scripts) without dependencies. After running `spark-submit`, the return code can be retrieved using `echo $?`.


```r
spark_version <- "3.0.0"

# test code without dependencies:
n <- 100
df <- data.frame(lapply(seq(10), function(c) sapply(runif(n = n, min = -2147483648, max = 2147483647), as.integer)))
colnames(df) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H", "I", "J")
sdf <- sdf_copy_to(sc, df, overwrite = TRUE)
tdf <- sdf_collect(sdf)

```

    --deploy-mode client \

title: Error using sparklyr on a Big Data Appliance
description:
Hi,

we are using sparklyr on a kerberized Oracle Big Data Appliance cluster from an edge node, but we can't use the two different methods tu submit jobs to spark (yarn-cluster and yarn-client) because we receive an error in both cases. In particular when we try to use the cluster-mode we receive the following error, and it is impossible to establish a connection:

```
Error in spark_yarn_cluster_get_resource_manager_webapp() :

  Failed to open bda1node05.ced.it:8033/ws/v1/cluster/info with status 404.
```
  
  
When we use the yarn-client submission we manage to create the connection and start the elaboration, but when we try to collect data to the driver we obtain the following error:
`Error: org.apache.spark.SparkException: Job aborted due to stage failure: Task 1 in stage 3.0 failed 4 times, most recent failure: Lost task 1.3 in stage 3.0 (TID 25, bda1node04.ced.it, executor 2): TaskResultLost (result lost from block manager)`

In this case we managed to complete the collect if we strongly limit the data that we are processing.


The cluster uses a CDH 5.14.3 with spark 2.2.0, R 4.0.2 and we are using the last version of sparklyr, the 1.5.1. Can you give us support into understanding what is the problems that we are facing?

We report some of the configurations that we tested in client-mode:
library(tidyverse)
library(sparklyr)
Sys.setenv("SPARK_HOME" = '/opt/cloudera/parcels/SPARK2/lib/spark2')
Sys.setenv("YARN_CONF_DIR" = '/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH/lib/spark/conf/yarn-conf')

conf$spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled<-FALSE
conf$spark.dynamicAllocation.minExecutors<-1
conf$spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors<-1
conf$spark.executor.instances<-1
conf$'sparklyr.shell.executor-memory'<- "20g"
conf$'sparklyr.shell.driver-memory'<- "50g"
conf$spark.memory.fraction<- "0.9"

title: zero-length key name in map type fails
description:
It is possible for maps to have zero-length keys. Although such a map is of limited value, I've run into real cases where this is the case and `sparklyr` gets angry about it. This can be reproduced via

```
iris_spk <- copy_to(sc, iris) # where sc is a spark connection
iris_spk %>%
  mutate(Species=if_else(Species=="setosa", "", Species)) %>% # drum up some empty keys
  group_by(Species) %>% 
  mutate(width_map=map(Species, Petal_Width)) %>% 
  collect() 
# Error in env[[key]] <- value : attempt to use zero-length variable name
```

It looks like maps are translated in the R as named lists. In the event of a zero-length name could that list entry simply not get a name?

I'm using `sparklyr` 0.8.4 with spark 2.3.1.

title: Spark SQL expressions in dplyr statements require double escaping
description:
Example data:
```
df <- data.frame(dep = "R (>= 2.15.0), xtable")
df_tbl <- sdf_copy_to(sc, df, overwrite = TRUE)
```

Let's say we want to capture the parenthesized content. We'd naturally try:
```
df_1 <- df_tbl %>%
  mutate(dep_new = regexp_replace(dep, "\\(([^)]+)\\)", "!"))
df_1
# # Source:   lazy query [?? x 2]
# # Database: spark_connection
# dep                   dep_new
# <chr>                 <chr>  
#   1 R (>= 2.15.0), xtable !)!  
```

This doesn't work because:
```
df_1 %>%
  dbplyr::sql_render()
# <SQL> SELECT `dep`, REGEXP_REPLACE(`dep`, "\(([^)]+)\)", "!") AS `dep_new`
# FROM `df`
```

Instead, we need to provide the extra `\`s:

```
df_2 <- df_tbl %>%
  mutate(dep_new = regexp_replace(dep, "\\\\(([^)]+)\\\\)", "!"))
df_2
# # Source:   lazy query [?? x 2]
# # Database: spark_connection
# dep                   dep_new    
# <chr>                 <chr>      
#   1 R (>= 2.15.0), xtable R !, xtable
df_2 %>%
  dbplyr::sql_render()
# <SQL> SELECT `dep`, REGEXP_REPLACE(`dep`, "\\(([^)]+)\\)", "!") AS `dep_new`
# FROM `df`
```

Behavior in Scala:
```
scala> val df = Seq("R (>= 2.15.0), xtable").toDF("dep")
df: org.apache.spark.sql.DataFrame = [dep: string]

scala> df.createOrReplaceTempView("mytable")

scala> spark.sql("""SELECT `dep`, REGEXP_REPLACE(`dep`, '\\(([^)]+)\\)', '!') AS `dep_new` FROM `mytable`""").show()
+--------------------+-----------+
|                 dep|    dep_new|
+--------------------+-----------+
|R (>= 2.15.0), xt...|R !, xtable|
+--------------------+-----------+


scala> spark.sql("""SELECT `dep`, REGEXP_REPLACE(`dep`, '\(([^)]+)\)', '!') AS `dep_new` FROM `mytable`""").show()
+--------------------+-------+
|                 dep|dep_new|
+--------------------+-------+
|R (>= 2.15.0), xt...|    !)!|
+--------------------+-------+
```

I dev-tools installed all of `dplyr`, `dbplyr`, and `sparklyr` just now (June 25, 2017) and tried to run the code below.  After about 10 repeats of the "rep" loop it hard-locks the `Spark` cluster (just a local cluster) with excessive GC load (I got a message from the HTML user interface once, and have pasted that below).  This is a re-worked example that should have no leaks if the `dplyr::db_drop_table()` steps are working, and should not have long dependencies if the `dplyr::compute()` steps are working.  Each repetition simulates `rbinding` about 12 tables for a final row count of less that 400 rows.   So even though we are repeating hundreds of steps- they are all supposed to be affordable steps.

#' Compute union_all of tables.  Cut down from \code{replyr::replyr_union_all()} for debugging.
#'
#' @param sc remote data source tables are on (and where to copy-to and work), NULL for local tables.
#' @param tabA not-NULL table with at least 1 row on sc data source, and columns \code{c("car", "fact", "value")}.
#' @param tabB not-NULL table with at least 1 row on same data source as tabA and columns \code{c("car", "fact", "value")}.
#' @return table with all rows of tabA and tabB (union_all).
#'
#' @export
example_union_all <- function(sc, tabA, tabB) {
  cols <- intersect(colnames(tabA), colnames(tabB))
  expectedCols <- c("car", "fact", "value")
  if((length(cols)!=length(expectedCols)) ||
     (!all.equal(cols, expectedCols))) {
    stop(paste("example_union_all: column set must be exactly",
               paste(expectedCols, collapse = ', ')))
  }
  mergeColName <- 'exampleunioncol'
  # build a 2-row table to control the union
  controlTable <- data.frame(exampleunioncol= c('a', 'b'),
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if(!is.null(sc)) {
    controlTable <- copy_to(sc, controlTable,
                            temporary=TRUE)
  }
  # decorate left and right tables for the merge
  tabA <- tabA %>%
    select(one_of(cols)) %>%
    mutate(exampleunioncol = as.character('a'))
  tabB <- tabB %>%
    select(one_of(cols)) %>%
    mutate(exampleunioncol = as.character('b'))
  # do the merges
  joined <- controlTable %>%
    left_join(tabA, by=mergeColName) %>%
    left_join(tabB, by=mergeColName, suffix = c('_a', '_b'))
  # coalesce the values
  joined <- joined %>%
    mutate(car = ifelse(exampleunioncol=='a', car_a, car_b))
  joined <- joined %>%
    mutate(fact = ifelse(exampleunioncol=='a', fact_a, fact_b))
  joined <- joined %>%
    mutate(value = ifelse(exampleunioncol=='a', value_a, value_b))
  joined %>%
    select(one_of(cols))
}

)

  for(i in (2:length(frameListS))) {

    prevNM <- nm

    count <- count + 1
    res <- compute(res, name=nm)
    dplyr::db_drop_table(sc, prevNM)
    print(paste(' done phase', rep, i, base::date()))

}

title: ft_vector_indexer() cannot handle invalid labels
description:
I have around 700 categorical features in my training set that I group into a vector using ft_vector_assembler() and then apply ft_vector_indexer(). Once this pipeline is fit via ml_fit() using the training set, I transform the validation set via ml_transform(). title: temporary spark_serialize_*.csv files don't get deleted
description:
Dear.
I'm using sparklyr to read hunderds of txt files process in R, copy the resulting dataframe into spark memory and write them to a parquet file.
Sparklyr creates this intermediate spark_serialize_*.csv files in the  /tmp folder in root.
However these files don't get deleted after the data is loaded into file.
Ofter 100's of files these add up to gigabytes and I run out of disk space in my root partition.
I'm not sure if it's expected behavior to keep this files in tmp or not?

I'm under the impression that these files are only created as an intermediate before loading an R data frame in to spark and that they are not needed afterwards.

Best

title: support spark 2.4
description:
Spark 2.4 brings lots of nice functionality (e.g., https://jira.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-23899) and seems to be released (https://archive.apache.org/dist/spark/spark-2.4.0/). Can sparklyr support this version?

Thanks much.

title: Reduce Dependencies
description: Various users have requested simplifying dependencies, clusters can take up to 30min to build. Ideally, `shiny` becomes suggested, not required, we only use Shiny on RStudio's UI for the connections pane and streams, so we should rather install Shiny from RStudio but not enforce it from `sparklyr`. We can also consider implementing `dplyr` generics but not a hard dependency. There might be other dependencies we can reduce.

title: Barriers
description:
[Spark 2.4](https://spark.apache.org/releases/spark-release-2-4-0.html) adds support for [RDD.barrier()](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/api/scala/org/apache/spark/rdd/RDD.html#barrier():org.apache.spark.rdd.RDDBarrier[T]) which is enabled by the new [Hydrogen scheduler](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LV4y7MPxIfA). Barriers are useful for parallel distributed processing, which can enable deep learning frameworks, as in, [Uber's Harovod](https://github.com/uber/horovod#usage), which already works in Spark, see [horovod-runner](https://docs.databricks.com/applications/deep-learning/distributed-deep-learning/horovod-runner.html).

Beyond Horovod, barriers could be particularly interesting to support many parallel computing packages available in R, see [State-of-the-art in Parallel Computing with R](https://www.open-mpi.org/papers/tr-uni-muenchen-8991/parallelR_techRep.pdf). Most of them work with MPI and support for MPI in Spark looks feasible now, see [spark-mpi/allreduce.py](https://github.com/SciDriver/spark-mpi/blob/master/examples/spark-mpi/allreduce.py). An overview of using barriers and MPI was presented in May 2018 under [Spark-MPI: Approaching the Fifth Paradigm of Cognitive Applications](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.01110.pdf).

While enabling `barrier()` in `sparklyr` might be as simple as adding a `barrier = T` parameter to trigger `rdd <- invoke(rdd, "barrier")` into `spark_apply()`, the more interesting work here would be to understand what we are missing to run Harovod and/or Spark-MPI in `sparklyr`.

title: Horovod
description:
- We need a `horovod` package that uses `reticulate` to match the `keras` package, etc.
- We also need a way to convert the `sparklyr` connection into a Horovod-ready connection. Seems horovod requires support for running a thread in Python that basically uses Open MPI, so we would have to support this and expose a python wrapper that is compatible with the rest of `horovod`, this is probably the trickiest piece.

title: Parallel connections to the gateway fail
description:
Hi,
I setup Spark to run in Standalone mode. Both Master and 1 Worker are located in the same machine and binds to localhost.

Now what I want to do is to start in parallel multiple sparklyr applications that should not share anything using gnu parallel. If I start them sequentially everything is fine, but if I lunch multiple of them at the same time some of the connections hang. On the masterweb page I don't see any application. the submit processes are spawned but either they do nothing or some of the connection attempts return 

> Error in force(code) : Failed while connecting to sparklyr to port (65530) for sessionid (73922): Sparklyr gateway did not respond while retrieving ports information after 60 seconds

As I understood, the backend is reused if already available, but maybe in this case a race condition rises. 
> If the port is already in use, the Backend will attempt to use the existing service running in this port as a sparklyr gateway and register itself. Therefore, the gateway socket serves not only as an interface to connect to the current instance, but also as bridge to other sparklyr backend instances running in this machine. This mechanism is the replacement of the ports file which used to communicate ports information back to the sparklyr client, in this model, one and only one gateway runs and provides the mapping between sessionids and ports. 

Or maybe my way of setting it up is wrong. Maybe in this scenario, I need one backend for eqach application. Here the code for reproducing

```r
library("sparklyr")
connect_to_spark <- function() {
  print(Sys.time())
  SPARK_MASTER <- "spark://127.0.0.1:7077"
  SPARK_HOME <- "/home/lorenzolucignano/spark-2.4.3-bin-hadoop2.7/"
  configuration <- spark_config()
  configuration$spark.sql.catalogImplementation <- "in-memory"
  configuration$sparklyr.gateway.timeout <- 5
  configuration$spark.driver.memory <- "1g"
  configuration$sparklyr.gateway.port <- 65530 
  configuration$spark.cores.max <- 1
  configuration$spark.driver.host <- "127.0.0.1"
  configuration$sparklyr.log.console <- TRUE
  configuration$spark.executor.memory<- "500m"
  return(spark_connect(master = SPARK_MASTER, spark_home = SPARK_HOME, config = configuration))
} 
sc<-connect_to_spark()
Sys.sleep(sample(seq(0.1,2,0.1), 1))
spark_disconnect(sc)
```

```sh
parallel Rscript spark_test.R ::: {1..100}
```

Using sparklyr 1.0.1.9004

Hi,

I am dealing with some unbalance dataset, so I want to do under-sampling before getting to any models. 
Here are my code:

```
balance <- data_tbl %>% group_by(Y) %>% summarise(n=n()) %>% collect   
  if(max(balance$n) > unbalance.cutoff*min(balance$n)){   
    data_tbl %<>%   
      group_by(Y)  %>%   
      sample_n(size = min(balance$n)) %>%    
      ungroup  
  }
```

The original data looks like this:

> A tibble: 2 × 2

> 

When running the above code in local mode, I got:

So, how to perform undersampling in sparklyr? Thanks.

title: update html reference on spark.rstudio.com
Unable to specify URL in spark_dependency jars argument
description:
For the [sparknlp](https://github.com/r-spark/sparknlp) extension I am maintaining there is a requirement that a URL is specified when creating the spark session for the `spark.jars` config parameter. (see example here: https://nlp.johnsnowlabs.com/docs/en/licensed_install#start-spark-nlp-for-healthcare-session-from-python)

Inside the package I have a `spark_dependencies()` function that returns a `spark_dependency` object containing packages and jars that need to be included in a spark session when it is created. That function looks something like this:

```r
spark_dependencies <- function(spark_version, scala_version, ...) {
   sparklyr::spark_dependency(jars = c("https://pypi.johnsnowlabs.com/######/spark-nlp-jsl-x.x.x.jar"),
                              packages = c("com.johnsnowlabs.nlp:spark-nlp_2.11:2.7.0"))
}
```
(note that a secret key is actually in the place of the ####### above)

when I try to open a spark connection I get this warning:

```
path[2]="https://pypi.johnsnowlabs.com/#######/spark-nlp-jsl-x.x.x.jar": No such file or directory
Backtrace:
 1. testthat::setup(...) testthat-tokenizer.R:1:0
 3. testthat_spark_connection() testthat-tokenizer.R:2:2
 4. sparklyr::spark_connect(...) helper-initialize.R:42:4
 5. sparklyr:::shell_connection(...)
 6. sparklyr:::start_shell(...)
 7. base::normalizePath(unlist(unique(all_jars)))
 ```

and then an error: `Error: Gateway in localhost:8880 did not respond`

It seems like something inside of sparklyr is assuming that the specification for the `jars` parameter to `spark_dependency` is a local file. 

If I specify this URL in the spark config (using `spark.jars`) when a user creates the spark connection it does work, but since it's a dependency of the sparknlp package the user should not have to do this.

title: performance regression in readDate method
description:
Collecting dataframes with date columns is about 300x slower in sparklyr 1.3 & 1.4 compared to version 1.2.

To reproduce the issue I created a temp view in spark with ~5 million rows with either a DateType or StringType. When a date type is included the collect time is much slower (~100x). This issue didn't exist in version 1.2. I profiled the code and it seems most of the execution time is spent in `readDate`, though I can't tell if it's actually something in readDate of the it's blocking on input from Spark.


Create temp views in spark:

```
val N = 5000000
val a = sc.parallelize((0 until N).map(i => MyDateRow(new Date(i * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)))).toDF
a.createOrReplaceTempView("tableWithDateColumn")
val b = sc.parallelize((0 until N).map(i => MyStringRow(new Date(i * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toString))).toDF
b.createOrReplaceTempView("tableWithStringColumn")
```

Query temp views:
```
# fast query
m <- sdf_sql(sc, "select * FROM tableWithStringColumn") %>% collect()

# slow query
m <- sdf_sql(sc, "select * FROM tableWithDateColumn") %>% collect()

```

title: databricks-connect : Relative path in absolute URI
description:
I can succesfully connect to Azure databricks from my local PC, with databricks-connect, but I cannot seem get the path to a mounted Azure Datalake Gen2 working. The code below all works fine if I run it on databricks in a notebook, but running it from my local RStudio doesn't work.

```r
source_delta <- "'dbfs:/mnt/investmentaccountingdata_dev/delta/bronze/rawdata/holdings/taxhld/v1.0'"
source_delta <- "/dbfs/mnt/investmentaccountingdata_dev/delta/bronze/rawdata/holdings/taxhld/v1.0"
source_delta <- "/mnt/investmentaccountingdata_dev/delta/bronze/rawdata/holdings/taxhld/v1.0"

df_bronze <- sparklyr::spark_read_delta(sc, path = source_delta, name = tbl_name_br, memory = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)
```
All 3 paths gives me the same error

> Error: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: java.net.URISyntaxException: Relative path in absolute URI: C:%5Cinndx%5Cprojects%5Cmartindut%5Cr_taxadmin%5C'dbfs:%5Cmnt%5Cinvestmentaccountingdata_dev%5Cdelta%5Cbronze%5Crawdata%5Choldings%5Ctaxhld%5Cv1.0'

It seems to try and translate the path to a local path on C:

This code works perfectly, but that's not how I want to run it
```r
source_delta <- "dbfs:/mnt/investmentaccountingdata_dev/delta/bronze/rawdata/holdings/taxhld/v1.0"
DBI::dbExecute(sc, paste0("CREATE TABLE ", tbl_name_br, " USING DELTA LOCATION '", source_delta, "'"))
```
I also tried this, but cannot get it working even if I set the configs 

```r
source_delta <- "abfss://investmentaccountingdata@xxxxxxxx.dfs.core.windows.net/delta/bronze/rawdata/holdings/taxhld/v1.0"
df_bronze <- sparklyr::spark_read_delta(sc, path = source_delta, name = tbl_name_br, memory = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)
```

> Error: com.databricks.service.SparkServiceRemoteException: Configuration property xxxxxxx.dfs.core.windows.net not found.

I tried setting the configs:
```r
config$fs.azure.account.auth.type.xxxxxxxx.dfs.core.windows.net <- "OAuth"
config$fs.azure.account.oauth.provider.type.xxxxxxxx.dfs.core.windows.net <- "org.apache.hadoop.fs.azurebfs.oauth2.ClientCredsTokenProvider"
config$fs.azure.account.oauth2.client.id.xxxxxxxx.dfs.core.windows.net <- "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
config$fs.azure.account.oauth2.client.secret.xxxxxxxx.dfs.core.windows.net <- "xxxxxxxx"
config$fs.azure.account.oauth2.client.endpoint.xxxxxxxx.dfs.core.windows.net <- endpoint
```
but no luck


First prize will be if I can just get the path to the mounted drive working, if I run the code from my local PC when connected with databricks-connect. Thanks

title: can't "copy_to" large datasets
description:
I try to copy somewhat large (~800MB) datasets into a Spark-Dataframe for benchmarking purposes. The data consists of one column with random numbers. Everything works well with smaller datasets, but at a specific point I just get the progressbar in the commandline, which goes up to 100% and then nothing happens anymore. I am working on a server with 100+ GB Memory, and 16 cores. I even tried to specify the executor and driver memory by hand, but nothing works.

The config looks like this:
```
spark_connect(master="yarn-client",
   config = list(
     default = list(
       spark.submit.deployMode= "client",
       spark.executor.instances= 20, 
       spark.executor.memory= "2G",
       spark.executor.cores= 4,
       spark.driver.memory= "4G")))
```
If I then stop the script, I get the following warning:
```

Warning message:
In spark_web.spark_shell_connection(sc) :
  Spark UI URL not found in logs, attempting to guess.
```

I don't know with which information I should provide you, since there is no error message.

library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)

kms <- function(idLogs){
    
    km  <- sparklyr::ml_kmeans(x = idLogs, centers = 3,features = c("latitude","longitude"))

    cluster <- sdf_predict(km)
    
    clustCounts <- cluster %>% group_by(prediction) %>% 
      tally  %>%
      mutate(conf=n/sum(n),
             prediction=prediction+1)
    
    clustCounts <- merge(clustCounts, km$centers, by.x=3, by.y=0)
    
    clustCounts <- clustCounts %>% filter(., conf==max(conf)) %>% select(latitude, longitude, conf)

    return(data.frame(clustCounts))
}

timeRanges <- c("7-17", "17-5")

Sys.setenv(HIVE_HOME="/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH/lib/hive/")

conf$sparklyr.worker.gateway.address = '127.0.0.1'

                    version="1.6.0",

                    config=list())

spark_read_csv extremely slow in comparison to read.df
description:
I have a storage account on Azure with enormous amount of csv files. I have configured spark to be able to access the storage account.

The following code takes hours and never ends:

```r
tic()
raw <- sc %>% spark_read_csv(
  "df",
  url,
  columns = schema,
  memory = F,
  headers = F,
  infer_schema = F)
toc()
```
and the corresponding sparkR (and scala) code has no problems:
```r
tic(); raw <- read.df(url, schema = schema, inferSchema = "false", source = "csv", header = "false"); toc()
```

Am I doing something wrong or is sparklyr unable to handle multiple files?

title: Error using distinct as intermediate step

title: Jar dependencies listed in `livy_config(jars=...)` are ignored
description:
Hi

I'm using sparklyr v1.5.0 with a Livy connection to an existing remote Spark cluster (old Spark 2.3.0, Cloudera HDP) and I've had troubles specifying jar dependencies for my code, as in the code below. Because the cluster has no outgoing access to internet (Github), I have prealably uploaded the required jars to HDFS.

```r
library(sparklyr)
SPARK_VERSION <- "2.3.0"
LIVY_SERVER <- "http://some.server:8999"

lcfg <- livy_config(
  negotiate = TRUE, custom_headers = list("X-Requested-By"=toupper(USER)), 
  jars = c(
    "hdfs:///users/pierre/jar/spark-sql-kafka-0-10_2.11-2.3.0.jar",  # Some Spark extension
    "hdfs:///users/pierre/jar/my-custom-package.jar" # Some personal code specific to my data model
))
lcfg$sparklyr.livy.jar = "hdfs:///users/pierre/jar/sparklyr-2.3-2.11.jar"  # Sparklyr server jar (from Github)

sc <- spark_connect(
  master = LIVY_SERVER, method = "livy", 
  version = SPARK_VERSION,
  config = lcfg)
```

As such, the jars listed in `livy_config(...)` are ignored and only `sparklyr.livy.jar` is actually included in the REST request creating the session. If I understand correctly the doc of `livy_config(...)`, this seems like a bug (?) 

Related issues about the link between livy.jars and sparklyr.livy.jar: #2722 and #2776 

I could find a simple fix, see PR below. Does it seem OK?

Thanks
Pierre

title: dbplyr 2.0.0 schema handling
description:
When using sparklyr 1.4.0 with dbplyr 2.0.0, some basic table operations fail, possibly due to the change in schema handling from dbplyr. 


It used to be able to access a Hive table using a character string specifying schema and table, but now it fails:

```r
tbl(sc, "schema_name.table_name") 
Error: org.apache.spark.sql.AnalysisException: Table or view not found: ...
```

The workaround I found was:

```r
tbl(sc, dbplyr::in_schema("edw_enc", "edw_product_line"))
tbl(sc, dbplyr::in_schema(sql("edw_enc"), sql("edw_product_line")))
```

Also `tbl_cache` is another one that I found. It used to work with:

```r
tbl_cache(sc, dbplyr::in_schema("edw_enc", "edw_product_line"))
```

But now it fails. 

Using character still works for `tbl_cache()`, i.e. 
```r
tbl_cache(sc, "schema_name.table_name")
```

The relevant dbplyr feature seems to be from [this commit](https://github.com/tidyverse/dbplyr/commit/b420776d116141f4ab7bafc77dd4465d9843b5e7), where the return of `in_schema` is now a list instead of a character vector. 


Thanks!

title: Livy tests failing
cache Apache Spark tar files in CI workflow
Strings with "NA" still handled incorrectly in sdf_copy_to
description:
Problem: 

When copying a data frame into spark, sdf_copy_to (or spark?) is treating characters or factors that use "NA" as NA. At least in R, "NA" is not the same as NA. Thus the copy in spark may have more NAs than it should. 

This appears related to https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/pull/1854. 

Example:
```r
sc <- spark_connect()

na_dat <- data.frame(A = rep("NA", times = 10),
                     B = c(rep("NA", times =5), rep(NA, times = 5)),
                     C = c(rep("C", times = 5), rep("NA", times = 3), rep(NA, times = 2)),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
na_dat_spark <- sdf_copy_to(sc = sc, x = na_dat, name = "na_dat", 
                          repartition = 8)
na_dat # A has zero NAs; B has 50% NAs; C has 20% NAs.
na_dat_spark # A and B are all NAs; C is 50% NAs
```

title: Problem with providing jars as part of spark loading thru sparklyr spark_connect and loading properly
description:

Previously, with sparklyr 1.0.2 - a connection w/ livy jars can be done this way, and a class that is contained in the jar file can be loaded without issues.  NOTE: the code is not using the `version` tag when using `spark_connect`

There are a few more things that I had tested, but I do not see the jar files passed to livy. 

The only sort of "success" was that - I can see the list of jars passed to livy during the session creation via this method, but then that causes the exception below.
```

title: weighted average function
description:
I'm trying to write a weighted average function that ignores the NA. As Spark SQL already has some basic aggregation function, I'm wondering whether there is a good way to invoke those functions and pack them into other R equivalent functions such as weighted.mean. 

---
```r
spark_version <- "2.1.0"
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", version = spark_version)
df <- data.frame(A = as.numeric(c(1, 0, NA, 2)), 
                 B = as.numeric(c(0, NA, 1, 3)), 
                 w = as.numeric(c(1, 1, 1, 1))
                 )
tbl <- copy_to(sc, df)
tbl %>% summarise(
  A_avg = sum(A * w, na.rm = T)/sum(w * as.numeric(!is.na(A)), na.rm = T), 
  B_avg = sum(B * w, na.rm = T)/sum(w * as.numeric(!is.na(B)), na.rm = T))
)
```
It would be nice to have: 

```r
weighted_avg <- function(A, w){
  sum(A * w, na.rm = T)/sum(w * as.numeric(!is.na(A)), na.rm = T)
}


tbl %>% summarise(
  A_avg = weighted_avg(A, w), 
  B_avg = weighted_avg(B, w)
  )
```

Thanks!

title: Using multiple functions with spark_apply
description:
Hello everyone, I'm applying a custom-made R function on a Spark dataframe using ```spark_apply``` but the issue that I'm facing is that the main function uses several other custom-made functions implemented in another local R script, in pseudo-code, my use-case looks like the following:

```
# where my sub-functions are located
source(functions.R)

# my main function that needs to be parrallelized
main_function <- function(data) {
   # calling a bunch of functions defined in functions.R
   call sub_function_1(data)
   call sub_function_2(data)
   ...
   call sub_function_n(data)
}

result <- spark_apply(spark_df, main_function)
```
My job crashes because worker nodes do not have a reference to the sub-functions. Indeed checking the worker nodes logs yields:

20/11/10 12:56:42 ERROR sparklyr: RScript (8197) terminated unexpectedly: could not find function "sub_function_1" 

By looking at the documentation, it seems that one possible way to cope with this is to supply the functions to the argument ```context``` of spark_apply but I've seen no examples with multiples functions and it doesnt'feel very practical given the fact that I have in total 8 sub-functions called within my main function which sums up to about 800 lines of code.

I saw that you can run a custom script before launching Rscript using ```sparklyr.apply.options.rscript.before``` so I've tried adding the following line to ```config-template.yml``` : 

```
sparklyr.apply.options.rscript.before:  "path/to/functions.R"
```
But this fails with the error message:
java.io.IOException: Cannot run program "path/to/functions.R" (in directory "."): error=2, No such file or directory

Can you please advise on what the best course of action is? 

Many thanks

title: sparklyr does not use `order_by` argument in lead/lag
description:
Dplyr offers the argument `order_by` for the `lead` and `lag` functions. 
Sparklyr does not seem to use this argument but instead requires that the table is ordered before (by using `arrange` before usage of lead/lag).

I've stolen the example from the test suit (https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/blob/master/tests/testthat/test-dplyr-lead-lag.R) and modified it a bit...
```r
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attache Paket: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

spark_version <- "2.2.0"
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", version = spark_version)
example_df <- data_frame(ID = 1:12, Cat = rep(c(letters[1:3], ""), 3),
                         Numb = c(3, 9, NA, 5, 1, 6, NA, 4, 3, 9, 11, NA),
                         ROrder = 12:1)
example_df_tbl <- copy_to(sc, example_df, overwrite = TRUE)


example_df %>%
    arrange(ID) %>%
    filter(Numb == 9,
           lead(Cat, default = "", order_by = ROrder) == "a")
#> Warning in filter_impl(.data, quo): hybrid evaluation forced for `lead`.
#> Please use dplyr::lead() or library(dplyr) to remove this warning.
#> # A tibble: 2 x 4
#>      ID Cat    Numb ROrder
#>   <int> <chr> <dbl>  <int>
#> 1     2 b         9     11
#> 2    10 b         9      3

example_df_tbl %>%
    arrange(ID) %>%
    filter(Numb == 9,
           lead(Cat, default = "", order_by = ROrder) == "a") %>%
    collect() %>%
    lapply(function(x) ifelse(is.nan(x), NA, x)) %>%
    as_data_frame()
#> Error in lead(Cat, default = "", order_by = ROrder): unused argument (order_by = ROrder)
```

title: Support [ bracket indexing
description:
Hive supports extracting an element from an array using square bracket indexing. However if a square bracket is used in a `mutate()` or `summarize()` function, an error is thrown.

For example:
```r
spark_version <- "2.1.0"
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", version = spark_version)

iris_spk <- copy_to(sc, iris, "iris")

iris_nested <- iris_spk %>%
  select(Species, Sepal_Length) %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarize(Sepal_Length=collect_list(Sepal_Length)) 

iris_nested %>%

title: create Spark equivalent of expand.grid
description:
Seems like a good idea to implement this as a convince helper method as part of the sparklyr sdf interface. Thanks to @nathaneastwood for suggesting it!

We need to be mindful of the following though:
- Things that exist for R dataframes but not for Spark dataframes: factors and attributes
- Decisions that are potentially important (performance-wise) in Spark but have no equivalent in R: whether to cache the resulting Spark dataframe in memory (or at least attempt to do so and give up if the resulting dataframe is too large), whether to include hints for broadcast hash join on some non-large dataframes in the crossjoin operation

title: fix broken tests possibly related to dbplyr 2.0.0
use protobuf to transport data from R to Spark faster
description:
- There is a prototype of this waiting to be developed into a complete protocol and fully tested
- Probably will only work with Spark 3.0 though due to Scala version issues
- Can probably use protobuf for faster transport in the opposite direction as well
- This doesn't mean protobuf is necessarily a superior binary serialization protocol... It just happens to have less overhead when serialization is happening in R/C++ and deserialization is happening in Scala. Avoiding excessive overhead in R and in Scala is quite tricky. Just re-writing some of sparklyr's R implementation in C++ did not help much either because calling C++ functions from R has its own overhead as well.

title: sdf_seq() error: `repartition` cannot be casted to an integer vector
description:
`sparklyr::sdf_seq()` will not work with the default `repartition` parameter. This is because it gets passed `type` which by default is one of `"integer"` or `"integer64"`, a character string.

```r
sparklyr::sdf_seq(sc)                                                                                                                                                       
# Error: `repartition` cannot be casted to an integer vector.
```

Also, "casted" is not a word; it should say "cast" - though this is a problem for the forge package.

Looking into the code, `repartition` gets passed to `cast_scalar_integer()` which in turn passes it to `case_integer()`.

title: How to parallelize database calls with registerDoSpark()?
description:
Does `sparklyr` need a function which is analogous to `doParallel::clusterEvalQ`?

I am trying to parallelize some database queries, where each worker would pull a single day's worth of data from the database, perform some calculations and then return the combined results. When I attempt to set this up, I receive an object not found error message for the database connection object. doParallel [has a similar problem](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/36759058/fetching-data-in-parallel-from-mysql-using-r-doparallel-or-foreach), which is solved by using `doParallel::clusterEvalQ` to initialize the database connection object onto the workers. 

```
library(tidyverse)
library(sparklyr)
library(foreach)

analysis_end_date   <- Sys.Date() - 1
analysis_start_date <- analysis_end_date - 60

creds <- config::get()

config <- spark_config()

sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", config = config)

jdbc_read_url <- config %>%
  glue::glue_data("jdbc:redshift://{host_url}:{port}/{db_name}") %>%
  as.character()

data_query <- glue::glue_sql(
  "SELECT * FROM sample_table
   WHERE date >= {analysis_start_date} AND date <= {analysis_end_date}",
   .con = DBI::ANSI()) %>% # Use ANSI connection for proper date quotes
  as.character()

database_tbl <- sc %>%
  spark_read_jdbc(sc      = .,
                  name    = "sample_table",
                  options = list(url      = jdbc_read_url,
                                 user     = creds$user_name,
                                 password = creds$password,
                                 query    = data_query,
                                 driver   = "com.amazon.redshift.jdbc42.Driver"),
                  memory  = FALSE)

analysis_calendar <- analysis_start_date %>%
  seq.Date(analysis_end_date, by = "day") %>%
  magrittr::extract(1:10)

registerDoSpark(sc)

foreach_results <- foreach(i = analysis_calendar,
          .export   = c("jdbc_read_url", "database_tbl"), 
          .packages = c("dplyr")) %dopar% {
          
  database_tbl %>%
                filter(date %in% i) %>%
                summarise(max_date = max(date, na.rm = TRUE),
                avg_mpg  = mean(mpg, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
               collect()
}
```

When I run the code above, I get...
```
Error in <bytecode> : 
  task 1 failed - "java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Object not found 18
	at sparklyr.StreamHandler.handleMethodCall(stream.scala:110)
	at sparklyr.StreamHandler.read(stream.scala:61)
```
Which, I think, means spark is looking for the `database_tbl` object and is unable to find it. 

Does `sparklyr` have (need?) a way to create database connections on all of the worker nodes, so that the foreach loop can retrieve the queries?

title: Reading from kafka topic stops aggregation query from publishing into topic
description:
Hi,

I am facing a puzzling issue when trying to read aggregates i publish into kafka topic. 

```r
library(sparklyr.confluent.avro)
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)

kafkaUrl <- "broker:9092"
sc <- spark_connect(master = "spark://spark-master:7077", spark_home = "spark")
stream_read_kafka(sc, options=list(kafka.bootstrap.servers=kafkaUrl, subscribe="parameter")) %>%
sdf_register("parameter")
"select value from parameter" %>%
dbplyr::sql() %>%
tbl(sc, .) %>%
mutate(value=as.character(value)) %>%
stream_watermark() %>%
group_by(time=window(timestamp, "5 minutes", "30 seconds"))%>%
summarise(n_new=n()) %>%
sdf_separate_column("time", into=c("start", "end")) %>%
select(-time) %>%
mutate(value=as.character(n_new))%>%
stream_write_kafka(options=list(kafka.bootstrap.servers=kafkaUrl, topic="aggregate"), mode='complete') 

# up to here it is fine, aggregate is being populated
s <- stream_read_kafka(sc, options=list(kafka.bootstrap.servers=kafkaUrl, subscribe="aggregate"))

# if i print s, it stops producing into the aggregate topic
```

Reading the aggregate topic above stops the continuous query from publishing to aggregate topic. Any idea what is going on ? I can provide a fully reproducible example if need be (vagrant/docker/python) but i think it is not specific to what i am doing.

title: yarn-cluster not respecting application name
description:
---

Providing ```app_name``` is not respected by Yarn when ```master     = "yarn-cluster"```, although the name is registered properly with Spark. Yarn always registers the application name as ```sparklyr.Shell```:

```r
library(sparklyr)
Sys.setenv(JAVA_HOME = '/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-11.0.8.10-0.el7_8.x86_64')
Sys.setenv(SPARK_HOME = '/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH/lib/spark/')
Sys.setenv(YARN_CONF_DIR = '/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH/lib/spark/conf/yarn-conf/')

sc <- spark_connect(app_name = "yarn_name_debug",master = "yarn-cluster")
```

title: dplyr mutate: Error: org.apache.spark.sql.AnalysisException: cannot resolve 'Name' given input columns:

# Reporting an Issue with sparklyr

I'm working on a project that needs a huge number of mutation for the cleansing and transformation phases using 
**mutate** and **regexp_replace** functions
But what I see, there is a limitation for using mutate, in the below example If you reduce the number of mutate function, the example will work fine, but if you keep it as is, you will get the following error
`

`

---

My reproducible example:

```r
conf <- spark_config()

conf$spark.driver.cores <- 2
conf$spark.executor.memory <- "8G"

make `sdf_weighted_sample` functionality available through the dplyr interface
description:
I think it can be done, but will be non-straightforward due to the fact that a Spark SQL UDF cannot have data frame as its return type.

At SQL query generation time:
- Sparklyr generates random name for a temp view that will store the sampling result
- Then generates a UDF invocation passing this temp view name and other sampling params to a UDF that will run the weighted sampling Scala method to populate the temp view with samples
- Finally generates a select query on the temp view containing sample result

At SQL query runtime:
 - First the temp view is populated with sample results
 - And then a select query returns the results

title: Inconsistent dates depending on whether arrow package is loaded

Importing dates from Spark results in erroneous dates unless the arrow package is loaded. This is probably related to #1954 and #1517. I suspect it is also related to timezones, but it is not obvious to me why a timezone difference between Spark and the R session would affect dates in this manner. 

```r
library(sparklyr)

if ("arrow" %in% .packages()) detach("package:arrow")
Sys.timezone() # America/Los_Angeles
df <- data.frame(date_orig = as.character(seq(as.Date("2019-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 12)))

sdf <- copy_to(sc, df, overwrite = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date_class = as.Date(date_orig)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date_internal = as_date(date_orig)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date_class_chr = as.character(date_class)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date_internal_chr = date_format(date_internal, "yyyy-MM-dd z"))

sdf %>% collect() # April through November are wrong for the date_class, date_internal

library(arrow)
sdf %>% collect() # Correct result

title: unnest.tbl_spark is buggy
description:
I realize that `unnest.tbl_spark` was merged yesterday and may not be considered complete, but as #1233 was closed I figured I'd post some feedback.

Setup:
```
sc <- spark_connect()

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(sparklyr)
library(sparklyr.nested)

# some test data
iris2 <- copy_to(sc, iris, name="iris")

# nested structs
iris_struct <- iris2 %>%
  sdf_nest(Sepal_Length, Sepal_Width, .key = "Sepal") %>% 
  sdf_nest(Petal_Length, Petal_Width, .key = "Petal")
head(iris_struct, 2)
#> # Source: spark<?> [?? x 3]
#>   Species Sepal            Petal           
#>   <chr>   <list>           <list>          
#> 1 setosa  <named list [2]> <named list [2]>
#> 2 setosa  <named list [2]> <named list [2]>

# nested arrays
iris_array <- iris_struct %>%
  sdf_nest(Sepal, Petal, .key = "Measurements") %>% 
  group_by(Species) %>% 
  summarize(Measurements = collect_list(Measurements))
```
In what follows `sdf_nest` and `sdf_unnest` are from the `sparklyr.nested` package (which I would be only too happy to deprecate when the functionality is eclipsed by `sparklyr`) I show them here to compare their behavior with the behavior in `unnest`.

It seems that despite the error message requesting "struct" types, it doesn't actually work well with struct fields. I believe that the [`explode_outer`](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/api/sql/index.html#explode_outer) function used under the hood wants arrays, not structs.
```
iris_struct %>% 
  sdf_unnest(Sepal, keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  head(2)
#> # Source: spark<?> [?? x 4]
#>   Species Petal            Sepal_Length Sepal_Width
#>   <chr>   <list>                  <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 setosa  <named list [2]>          5.1         3.5
#> 2 setosa  <named list [2]>          4.9         3

iris_struct %>% 
  unnest(Sepal) %>% 
  head(2)
#> Error: Unnesting is only supported for struct type columns. Column 'Sepal' is of type StructType(StructField(Sepal_Length,DoubleType,true), StructField(Sepal_Width,DoubleType,true))
```

If I work with arrays (measurements grouped by species) it seems to work well, until I want to pull values out of the structs within the arrays.
```
iris_array %>% 
  sdf_unnest(Measurements, keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  head(2)
#> # Source: spark<?> [?? x 3]
#>   Species   Sepal            Petal           
#>   <chr>     <list>           <list>          
#> 1 virginica <named list [2]> <named list [2]>
#> 2 virginica <named list [2]> <named list [2]>

iris_array %>% 
  sdf_unnest(Measurements, keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  sdf_unnest(Sepal, keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  sdf_unnest(Petal, keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  head(2)
#> # Source: spark<?> [?? x 5]
#>   Species   Sepal_Length Sepal_Width Petal_Length Petal_Width
#>   <chr>            <dbl>       <dbl>        <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 virginica          6.3         3.3          6           2.5
#> 2 virginica          5.8         2.7          5.1         1.9

iris_array %>% 
  unnest(Measurements) %>% 
  head(2)
#> # Source: spark<?> [?? x 3]
#>   Species   Sepal            Petal           
#>   <chr>     <list>           <list>          
#> 1 virginica <named list [2]> <named list [2]>
#> 2 virginica <named list [2]> <named list [2]>

iris_array %>% 
  unnest(Measurements) %>% 
  unnest(c(Sepal, Petal)) %>% 
  head(2)
#> Error: Unnesting is only supported for struct type columns. Column 'Sepal' is of type StructType(StructField(Sepal_Length,DoubleType,true), StructField(Sepal_Width,DoubleType,true))
```

I think the gist here is that `unnest` is implemented to be equivalent to spark `explode`, but `tidyr::unnest` is more than that. It will explode (`unnest_longer`) _and_ do a nested select (`unnest_wider`). The nested selection (i.e., promote fields in structs to the top level) is not working here.

title: Data frames being overwritten if the files being read from databricks mount have same filename
description:
So we are trying to read 2 files from a mounted storage in databricks using sparklyr. Both the files have same file name but different paths. And we are obviously reading them in different dataframe variables. 

Now the problem is that the variables are somehow getting overwritten and both the variables become equal to the last data set being loaded. If the file names are different then we do not see this issue. Additionally this issue seems to be specific to sparklyr as we tried to replicate this with SparkR and in Python as well but they behave as expected. 

Databricks Runtime - 7.1 & 6.5

```r
library(sparklyr)

sc <- spark_connect(method = "databricks")

data1 <- spark_read_parquet(sc, path = "dbfs:/mnt/datalake/path1/filename.parquet")

sdf_nrow(data1)

data2 <- spark_read_parquet(sc, path = "dbfs:/mnt/datalake/path2/filename.parquet")

sdf_nrow(data2)

sdf_nrow(data1)

```

title: Sparkly throws URISyntaxException when connecting to spark via Livy using spark 2.4
description:
### Sparkly throws URISyntaxException when connecting to spark via Livy using spark 2.4. 

**1. How to reproduce this issue.**
```r
conf <- spark_config()   # Load variable with spark_config()
conf$`sparklyr.cores.local` <- 2
conf$`sparklyr.shell.driver-memory` <- "8G"
conf$spark.executor.memory <- "4G"
conf$spark.executor.cores <- 2
conf$spark.executor.instances <- 3
conf$spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled <- "false"
sc <- spark_connect(
  master = "http://192.168.0.6:8998",
  version = "2.4",
  method = "livy", config = conf)
```

**2. Errors**
```
Error in livy_validate_http_response("Failed to create livy session", : Failed to create livy session (Client error: (400) Bad Request):

 {"msg":"java.net.URISyntaxException: Illegal character in scheme name at index 1: 
c(\"https://github.com/sparklyr/sparklyr/blob/feature/sparklyr-1.3.0/inst/java/sparklyr-2.4-2.11.jar?raw=true\", \"https://github.com/sparklyr/sparklyr/blob/feature/sparklyr-1.3.0/inst/java/sparklyr-2.4-2.12.jar?raw=true\")"}

title: unexpected behavior with dplyr arrange
description:
Using sparklyr within databricks I often use group_by, arrange, ungroup.  Recently, sparklyr has started retaining arranges when I would not expect it to. 

An example from databricks:

```library(dplyr)
library(sparklyr)

sc <- spark_connect(method = 'databricks')

#turn mtcars into spark df
mtcars <- sdf_copy_to(sc, mtcars, overwrite = TRUE)

mtcars_arrange <- mtcars %>% 
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  arrange(wt) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(mpg, cyl, gear)
```

when I glimpse the dataframe resulting from above, it reports to be ordered by wt:
```
Observations: ??
Variables: 3
Database: spark_connection
Ordered by: wt
$ mpg  <dbl> 30.4, 30.4, 33.9, 27.3, 26.0, 32.4, 22.8, 21.5, 21.0, 19.7, 21.4…
$ cyl  <dbl> 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 6, 6, 4, 6, 4, 8, 4, 6, 8, 6, 8, 6, 6, 8…
$ gear <dbl> 5, 4, 4, 4, 5, 4, 4, 3, 4, 5, 4, 4, 4, 5, 4, 3, 3, 4, 3, 4, 3, 3…
```

When attempting to do further analysis/calculations, this ordered by wt results in errors: 

```
mtcars_arrange %>%

title: Configuration via `sparklyr.shell.*` or `spark.*`
description:
I was trying to connect in YARN client mode and wanted to configure my executor and driver memory. I followed [this chapter](https://therinspark.com/tuning.html#tuning-configuring) in the R in Spark book and tried to configure `sparklyr.shell.*` options instead of `spark.*` options. See a minimal connection setting below.

```r
library(sparklyr)
conf <- spark_config()
conf$`sparklyr.shell.executor-memory` <- "2g"
conf$`sparklyr.shell.driver-memory` <- "2g"

sc <- spark_connect(master = "yarn-client", config = conf)
```

After connected, in the web UI under executors, it seemed that **the driver took the memory setting but the executors didn't**. The 2 default executors had 384M storage memory while the driver had 956M. 

On the environment page, it shows the following spark-submit info:
```
org.apache.spark.deploy.SparkSubmit --conf spark.driver.memory=2g --class sparklyr.Shell --executor-memory 2g /had/home/a377324/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.5/sparklyr/java/sparklyr-2.0-2.11.jar 8880 11555
```

It seems like the `sparklyr.shell.driver-memory` was taken and then passed as `sparklyr.shell.driver-memory` in the `--conf` flag, but executor memory is passed as a spark-submit flag and wasn't honored. I didn't quite understand the difference here... When I try to set `spark.executor.memory` instead (as suggested [here](https://spark.rstudio.com/guides/connections/)), it seems to be getting 2g correctly. Should I be using the `sparklyr.shell.*` options, or the `spark.*` options, or both?
