title: dplyr compute() Bug
description:
@javierluraschi 

I'm running into an issue with a script I'm writing where it looks like `compute()` isn't forcing computation of a table.  After executing the `compute` method, when filtering on the subsequent table I'm running into errors that appear to be referencing some lazy evaluation of a join that was done prior to running `compute`.  From the documentation, it doesn't seem like this should happen (unless I'm misinterpreting something).  

I was able to recreate it with a generic script which is below so you can see the behavior.

```
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)
library(titanic)


# ----------------------------
# Connect to Spark
# ----------------------------
Sys.setenv(SPARK_HOME = "/usr/lib/spark")

sc <- spark_connect(master = "yarn-client", version = '2.0.1')
# spark_disconnect(sc)


# ----------------------------
# Import Data
# ----------------------------
titanic_tbl <- copy_to(sc, df = titanic_train, name = "titanic", overwrite = TRUE)

passenger_exclude <- data.frame(passenger_excl = c(1, 5, 7))
passenger_exclude_tbl <- copy_to(sc, df = passenger_exclude, name ="pass_exc", overwrite = TRUE)


# ----------------------------
# Prepare dataset and train model
# ----------------------------
titanic_final_tbl <- titanic_tbl %>%
    mutate(Age = ifelse(is.na(Age), mean(Age), Age)) %>%
    select(PassengerId, Survived, Pclass, Sex, Age, SibSp, Parch, Fare)

model_frmla <- formula(Survived ~ Pclass + Sex + Age + SibSp + Parch + Fare)

# Train model
model <- ml_logistic_regression(titanic_final_tbl, model_frmla)


# ----------------------------
# Eliminate some records that are not needed
# ----------------------------
titanic_test_clean_tbl <- left_join(titanic_final_tbl, passenger_exclude_tbl,  by = c("PassengerId" = "passenger_excl")) %>%
    sdf_register("titanic_test_join")

titanic_test_final_tbl <- titanic_test_clean_tbl %>%
    filter(is.na(passenger_excl)) %>%  #exclude any record that was present in passenger_exclude_tbl
    sdf_register("titanic_test_final")


# ----------------------------
# Score Test file
# ----------------------------
score_tbl <- sdf_predict(model, titanic_test_final_tbl) %>%
    select(PassengerId, prediction, probability) %>%
    sdf_register("score_output")


# Check Score Numbers
score_tbl %>%
    filter(prediction == 1) %>%
    group_by(prediction) %>%
    summarise(count = n())


# ----------------------------
# Results in error which mentions join... assume this has to do with lazy evaluation.
# Lets try using compute() first
# ----------------------------

compute(titanic_test_final_tbl, "compute_test")
compute_tbl <- tbl(sc, "compute_test")


# Score Test file

score_tbl <- sdf_predict(model, compute_tbl) %>%
    select(PassengerId, prediction, probability) %>%
    sdf_register("score_output")


# Check Score Numbers
score_tbl %>%
    filter(prediction == 1) %>%
    group_by(prediction) %>%
    summarise(count = n())


# ----------------------------
# Still get the error... it looks like compute() is not really forcing the lazy eval to calc
# Lets try caching the table
# ----------------------------

tbl_cache(sc, name = "titanic_test_final")

# Score Test file

score_tbl <- sdf_predict(model, titanic_test_final_tbl) %>%
    select(PassengerId, prediction, probability) %>%
    sdf_register("score_output")


# Check Score Numbers
score_tbl %>%
    filter(prediction == 1) %>%
    group_by(prediction) %>%
    summarise(count = n())


# ----------------------------
# Caching seems to force the table to calculate.  
# Based on documentation, it looks like compute() should be doing this as well but its not
# ----------------------------
```

title: support for nested object / method access in 'invoke'?
description:
It might be useful to make it possible to invoke methods on sub-objects more simply with `invoke`, e.g. given a Spark DataFrame, it might be nice to write:

```
invoke(sdf, "na.drop")
```

rather than

```
sdf %>% invoke("na") %>% invoke("drop")
```

In other words, we could manually split the objects according to `.`s found in the string, and then execute the methods sequentially. Would this be useful, or could it lead to potential confusion? (Does Scala ever let you define methods / objects with names that contain a `.` -- I assume not?)

title: consider moving derby.log and log4j.log into different directory
description:
`sparklyr` uses the current directory which creates a couple extra logging files: `darby.log` and `log4j.log`.

While this can be redirected by changing the following files:

`~/Library/Caches/spark/<spark-version>/conf/log4j.properties`

and this spark config:

``` r
config[["sparklyr.shell.conf"]] <- "spark.executor.extraJavaOptions=-Dderby.stream.error.field=DerbyUtil.DEV_NULL"
```

it would be preferable not to pollute the current directory.

title: Another Column Limit Issue
consider setting spark.sql.warehouse.dir by default
description:
See: https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/issues/229#issuecomment-251584060

Some users have reported that in order to get `dplyr` and `sparklyr` to work in windows, they need to set `spark.sql.warehouse.dir` as follows to unblock a Hive exception:

``` r
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)
sc <- spark_connect(master = "spark://address:7077", config = list(spark.sql.warehouse.dir = "d:/Spark2/tmp/hadoop/bin"))
iris_tbl <- copy_to(sc, iris)
```

It is worth considering setting this automatically to "SPARK_HOME/tmp/hadoop/bin" but this would require more investigation to understand if setting `spark.sql.warehouse.dir` is the right approach.

title: Dplyr query in tutorial not the same as on a data.frame
description:
Going over the tutorial [here](http://spark.rstudio.com/#rstudio-ide) and noticed that running this on sparklyr:

```
delay <- flights_tbl %>% 
  group_by(tailnum) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), dist = mean(distance), delay = mean(arr_delay)) %>%
  filter(count > 20, dist < 2000, !is.na(delay)) %>%
  collect()
```

Gives different results from:

```
flights_tbl  %>% collect() -> flights_df

delay_df <- flights_df %>% 
    group_by(tailnum) %>%
    summarise(count = n(), dist = mean(distance), delay = mean(arr_delay)) %>%
    filter(count > 20, dist < 2000)
```

It seems to be because the mean in spark has something like `na.rm = TRUE` by default.

description: [Model Formulae](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/formula.html) support additional terms like `:`, `^`, etc. Customers have reached out at least to support `:` but others should be considered.

title: Add support for anonymous Scala functions
description:
It would be useful if there could be some way to parse basic Scala code declared from R, such that the following types of call are possible:

``` r
new_data_frame <- 
  spark_dataframe(auto_data) %>% 
  invoke("map", "(x: Row) => x")
```

This would remove the need to perform basic data manipulation elsewhere so that all code could be kept in once place. 

I would like to be able to use Scala functions like `map` as we can't (currently) apply/mutate using native R functions (although the more I Iearn about `ft_sql_transformer()` and Hives' UDFs the less of a need this becomes). 

I've had a quick look through the Scala docs and can't figure-out how Scala creates lambda functions (in a vain attempt to refer to the underlying Java object). I understand that I couple compile a custom JAR and use the Extensions API, but I'm looking for something more on-the-fly, if at all possible.

title: Google Dataproc: Certain error conditions cause a hang in the command
description:
Using sparklyr 0.2.9 (but not new to this version)
- Bring up Google Dataproc Spark/Hadoop cluster
  I am using n1-standard-2, 7.5G RAM, 1 master and 2 worker nodes
  Not any change to the setup, expect for installing R,RSP, and packages
- Do the initial setup and connect to spark
  Note: I use `sc <- spark_connect(master = "yarn-client")` to connect. Connect using the hostname as master didn't work in this environment.
  Note: May be the configuration is not correct for our purposes, and leading to this issue. (I don't see this issue on the AWS cluster)
- As an example, running the following command to read a valid s3 path works fine after initial environment setup:

```
dpd <- spark_read_csv(sc, "dpd", "s3n://dallas-police/current.csv")
```

but if I change that to use an invalid bucket:

```
dpd1 <- spark_read_csv(sc, "dpd", "s3n://dallas-police1/current.csv")
```

then the command just hangs. I have waited for 10 minutes, nothing happened. At this point if you cancel the command then nothing else, even spark_disconnect wouldn't work.

I have seen this issue with some valid commands that for some reason didn't work in this environment. But here I am used an invalid command that should return an error pretty quickly.

There is no info in the log when I run spark_log(sc).

title: Rotate data using PCA components found
description:
# New functionality: Provide rotated data after PCA

Perhaps I have somehow missed this functionality, and if so apologies and it would be great if you could point me in the right direction, but at the moment I haven't been able to find a way to retrieve data as obtained after rotating by the PCA components found by ml_pca(): that is, the PCA components are easily accessible using $components, but the result of matrix multiplication of the input data by the PCA components doesn't seem to be accessible.

I have tried to go into ml_pca() and hack the input dataframe conversion into RowMatrix() and then do the multiplication to obtain the transformed data, but so far unsuccessfully.

If this functionality could be added, or if you can point me in the right direction to convert the data input in ml_pca() into a RowMatrix so I can do the matrix multiplication in Spark that would be great.

---

The desired output is the "projected" variable shown [here in the Spark documentation](https://spark.apache.org/docs/2.1.0/mllib-dimensionality-reduction.html#principal-component-analysis-pca):

val mat: RowMatrix = new RowMatrix(dataRDD)

// Compute the top 4 principal components.
// Principal components are stored in a local dense matrix.
val pc: Matrix = mat.computePrincipalComponents(4)

// Project the rows to the linear space spanned by the top 4 principal components.
val projected: RowMatrix = mat.multiply(pc)

title: Consider modifications to spark_apply group_by API
description:
For discussion... here are some ideas I have from playing with https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/pull/833

cc @javierluraschi @statmatt

1. The key(s) should come first in arguments for `f`. I think this is more natural.
2. Append grouping columns to resulting DataFrame by default. In practice they're almost always needed and users can easily deselect/rename otherwise.
3. Support grouping by multiple columns.

Sample test for these requirements:

```
s <- spark_apply(
  mtcars_tbl,
  function(cyl, gear, d) lm(mpg ~ disp, d)$coefficients[["(Intercept)"]],
  names = c("intercept"),
  group_by = list("cyl", "gear")
) %>% collect()

r <- mtcars %>%
  tidyr::nest(-cyl, -gear) %>%
  mutate(model = purrr::map(data, ~lm(mpg ~ disp, data = .)),
         intercept = purrr::map_dbl(model, function(x) x$coefficients[["(Intercept)"]])) %>%
  select(cyl, gear, intercept)

expect_equal(s, r)
```

4. Enforce function signature of `f` to be consistent with number of grouping columns. The user can give either 1 argument (for the data) or *n* where *n = number of grouping columns + 1*. So this would be OK:

```
s1 <- spark_apply(
  mtcars_tbl,
  function(cyl, gear, d) lm(mpg ~ disp, d)$coefficients[["(Intercept)"]],
  names = c("intercept"),
  group_by = list("cyl", "gear")
) %>% collect()

s2 <- spark_apply(
  mtcars_tbl,
  function(d) lm(mpg ~ disp, d)$coefficients[["(Intercept)"]],
  names = c("intercept"),
  group_by = list("cyl", "gear")
) %>% collect()

expect_equal(s1, s2)
```

But this would not:

```
expect_error(
  spark_apply(
    mtcars_tbl,
    function(cyl, d) lm(mpg ~ disp, d)$coefficients[["(Intercept)"]],
    names = "intercept",
    group_by = list("cyl", "gear")
  ),
  "'f' has incorrect number of arguments"
)
```

title: Cannot handle more than 16 concurrent users
description:
Probably the weirdest bug I've encountered in a long time - SparkR (and sparklyr, by extension) cannot handle more than 16 concurrent Spark sessions from a single machine under the default settings.

Whenever you start a Spark session, it attempts to bind a port for it's web UI. If the default port (4040) is already in use, it goes onto the next to the next one (4041), and then the next one (4042), until it finds a free port. Apparently sparkR's default setting is do this a mere 16 times and then exit with an error (which subsequently causes sparklyr's connection to fail). So this ends up meaning that only 16 users can launch a spark session at a time (not sure who thought this was a sensible default).

When connecting over sparklyr, the only diagnostic info is (instantaneous, appears upon trying to start a connection when there are already 16 sessions):
```{r}
Error in force(code) : 
  Failed during initialize_connection: No status is returned. Spark R backend might have failed.
```

When connecting with SparkR, it actually shows the full stack trace, which mentions that `spark.port.maxRetries` should be increased.

Anyhow, the solution is to bump sparklyr's default `spark.port.maxRetries` up to a more reasonable number, say 128. (For users coming here via google: `config$spark.port.maxRetries <- 128`)

(Yes, this is actually a bug with SparkR itself, but you guys have the potential to solve it for anyone using sparklyr, so I'm reporting it here.)

title: Feature Request: Write to JDBC
description:
Per @javierluraschi's request I'm opening this issue and migrating the discussion away from Gitter.

I'd like to write to database sources directly from Spark. Currently, I can import data from, say, MySQL, directly into Spark via `spark_read_jdbc()`. But, if I perform a calculation in Spark and then wanted to send the data back to MySQL and update a table, it looks like I would have to collect the data into R and then use one of the R/DBI/RMySQL functions to perform the writing.

Javier's comments

> Should be fairly straightforward to implement this wrapper, we basically need to write one of this 

> (https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/blob/602043e87085830365dbe876f684e62a3b8553d1/R/data_interface.R#L473-L541) but for these parameters: https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/blob/602043e87085830365dbe876f684e62a3b8553d1/R/data_interface.R#L564.

So, I propose `spark_write_jdbc()`

title: sparklyr/RStudio reports error on dplyr::copy_to()
description:
When I run the follow reprex I always see the message "Error: Column `database` must be length 1 or 1, not 0".  Doesn't seem to get printed in the reprex (so I think it is a Spark error demoted to a warning or a message which is not printed).

```r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("dplyr"))
packageVersion("dplyr")
#> [1] '0.7.0'
suppressPackageStartupMessages (library("sparklyr"))
packageVersion("sparklyr")
#> [1] '0.5.6'
sc <- spark_connect(master= 'local',
                    version = '2.1.0')
d <- data.frame(x=1:9,
                y=rep(c('a','b','c'),3))
d <- copy_to(sc, d, 'd')
##>> Error: Column `database` must be length 1 or 1, not 0
```

The error is in the RStudio Spark viewer.  Pressing refresh on the viewer repeats the error with a message pop-up on RStudio saying "Error R code execution error."  RSTudio version: 1.0.143 .

title: Values converted to zero when working with tables of more than 200 columns
description:
Our production Hadoop installation runs Spark 1.6.2 with Hadoop 2.7 and so I've created a local installation for code development with:

```r
sparklyr::spark_install("1.6.2")
```

However `sparklyr::spark_install()` only offers up to Hadoop 2.6. 

If I use this configuration (Spark 1.6.2, Hadoop 2.6), then all values in a table with more than 200 columns get converted to zero.  For example:

```r
library(sparklyr)
library(rsparkling)
library(dplyr)

spark_version <- "1.6.2"

# Run one of these depending on system
sc_local <- spark_connect(master = "local", version = spark_version)
sc_cluster <- spark_connect(master = "yarn-client", version = spark_version)

load_h2o <- function(df, sc, rows = nrow(df), cols = ncol(df)) {
  df <- df[1:rows, 1:cols]
  copy_to(sc, df, "df", overwrite = TRUE)
  df_tbl <- tbl(sc, "df")
  h2o_tbl <- as_h2o_frame(sc, df_tbl, strict_version_check=FALSE)
  return(h2o_tbl)
}

df <- as.data.frame(matrix(rep(1, 201*500), ncol=201))

# Resulting data frame contains all 1s as expected on cluster and local 
load_h2o(df, sc_local, cols = 200)
load_h2o(df, sc_cluster, cols = 200)

# Gives 0s on local Spark, 1s on cluster
load_h2o(df, sc_local, cols = 201)
load_h2o(df, sc_cluster, cols = 201)

```

This is a [known bug with Spark 1.6.2](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-16664) but because I can run the code successfully on our 1.6.2 cluster, I wonder if it's related to the Hadoop version.

title: sparklyr complains about "same name columns" in join with dplyr and Spark 1.6.2
description:
sparklyr complains about "same name columns" in join with dplyr and Spark 1.6.2, this is even with columns that are the join condition.  Example with outcome in [link](https://github.com/WinVector/replyr/blob/master/issues/copyissue162.md).

The issue is illustrated below.  Using the current CRAN versions of dplyr and sparklyr (as of 2017-03-30') we get an error message "Use Spark2" when there are any duplicate column names: even in the "by" columns (which are often deliberately the same).  The problem is in real production systems you can choose your version of dplyr and sparklyr, but you often can not choose your version of Spark as it is part of a possibly shared cluster.

``` r
library("dplyr")
```

``` r
packageVersion("dplyr")
```

    ## [1] '0.5.0'

``` r
library("sparklyr")
packageVersion("sparklyr")
```

    ## [1] '0.5.4'

``` r
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", 
                    version = "1.6.2")

d1 <- copy_to(sc, 
              data.frame(x=c('a','b'), y=c(1,2)),
              name= 'd1',
              overwrite = TRUE)
d2 <- copy_to(sc, 
              data.frame(x=c('b'), z=c(3)),
              name= 'd2',
              overwrite = TRUE)
```

``` r
left_join(d1, d2, by='x')
```

    ## Error in sql_join.spark_connection(con, from_x, from_y, type = query$type, : This dplyr operation requires a feature not supported in Spark 1.6.2 . Try Spark 2.0.0 instead or avoid using same-column names in joins.

``` r
left_join(d1, rename(d2, xb = x), by= c('x'='xb'))
```

title: Crash on r-session after serializing bad strings or critical Spark exceptions
description:
Follow up from https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/issues/780.

There are a few instances where something bad happens in Spark (see https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/issues/783 and https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/issues/780) which follows a termination of the backend and the r-session crashing while reading from the socket.

With this helper function...

```
spark_serialize_bad_string <- function(sc) {
  rc <- rawConnection(raw(), "r+")
  sparklyr:::writeString(rc, "sparklyr.SQLUtils")
  sparklyr:::writeBoolean(rc, TRUE)
  sparklyr:::writeString(rc, "getSQLDataType")

  # write args
  sparklyr:::writeInt(rc, 1)
  sparklyr:::writeType(rc, "character")
  utfVal <- enc2utf8("test")
  sparklyr:::writeInt(rc, as.integer(4)) # giant string should cause OOM
  writeBin(utfVal, rc, endian = "big", useBytes = TRUE)

  bytes <- rawConnectionValue(rc)
  close(rc)

  rc <- rawConnection(raw(0), "r+")
  sparklyr:::writeInt(rc, length(bytes))
  writeBin(bytes, rc)
  con <- rawConnectionValue(rc)
  close(rc)

  backend <- sc$backend
  writeBin(con, backend)

  returnStatus <- sparklyr:::readInt(backend)

  if (length(returnStatus) == 0)
    stop("No status is returned. The sparklyr backend might have failed.")
  if (returnStatus != 0) {
    # get error message from backend and report to R
    msg <- sparklyr:::readString(backend)
    withr::with_options(list(
      warning.length = 8000
    ), {
      stop(msg, call. = FALSE)
    })
  }
}
```

connect,

```
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", version = "2.1.0")

and then running the following a few times will crash the r-session...

spark_serialize_bad_string(sc)

The default code works before I install the newest edition of sparklyr a few days ago by typing:
**devtools::install_github("rstudio/sparklyr"**

I am wondering if there's any alternative way to fix this.

                 name='a',

title: Including grep, mataches, etc in mutate
description:
Guys, as the other thread for udf and dapply keeping going i wonder if we could try to implement some of the reg. expression into sparklyr. 

Ex. df %>% mutate( text1 = ifelse( col1 %like% "$ text $" , 1, 0 )  ) - this works fine but if the reg expression has multiple attributes and multiple options the like ifelse becomes nasty. 

Ex: df %>% mutate( text1 = ifelse( col1 %like% c("$ text $","$ text2 $")  , 1, 0 )  )  - doesnt work. also is case sensitive. also way less powerful than grep. 

I can create a function that parse the sql element and takes care of all of this but it won't be aligned with grep and or other dplyr syntax. So before i do that, can you let me know if this is something you can easily integrate?

title: Null values in Long columns are collected as -2^63

```
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)
sc = spark_connect(master = "local")

local_df = data.frame(numeric_column = c(NA, 2:5), string_column = letters[1:5])
spark_df = copy_to(sc, local_df, overwrite = TRUE)
spark_df_with_long = spark_df %>% ft_sql_transformer(sql = "select cast(numeric_column as long), string_column from __THIS__")
spark_df_with_long %>% collect()

spark_df_with_long %>% collect()

title: Feature request: it would be very handy to have an official way to get table name and data source.
description:
Feature request: it would be very handy to have an official way to get table name and data source.

Below I have a reprex showing example implementations of the two functions I would like ( table_name and data_source ) with ad-hoc implementations that work by looking directly into the dplyr 0.5.0 data structures (obviously not the right way for external code, as this is unlikely to be stable across different data providers and sparklyr/dplyr versions).

The utility is: if you have handle to remote data you may want to delete the underlying data at some point as part of a clean up. The data_source has the additional use for copy_to as is already an option in the dplyr join verbs.

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("dplyr"))
library("sparklyr")
my_db <- spark_connect(version='2.0.2', 
                       master = "local")
d <- copy_to(my_db, data.frame(x=1:3), 'dsparkname')

# would like a version of this function that works
# accross multiple dplyr data sources: 
#  Spark, PostgreSQL, RSQLite, ...
# should return NULL if d is local data (data.frame/ tibble)
# should return NULL if d is not a trivial query.
table_name <- function(d) {
  as.character(d$ops$x)
}

title: Feature request: something to pull apart ml_* probability columns.
description:
Many of the `sparklyr` machine learning methods return class probabilities in a column of vectors. That is for each row we have a vector that has a probability per-class.  `ml_logistic_regression` is one example.  I have a worked example of the problem here: 
https://github.com/WinVector/Examples/blob/master/SparkTips/VSlicing/VSlicing.md .

These column of vectors values are hard to work with if you need to stay "on Spark" (i.e. the data is too big to call dplyr::collect() on). `sdf_read_column()` doesn't seem to be answer either as it returns a very large list of spark_job results (a possibly too large and very opaque structure).

My feature request is a function something like the following a new function with signature:
  `sdf_slice_vector(dataHandle, columnNameToTakeFrom, indexToTake, columnNameToWriteTo)` .
This would be the equivalent of of running the following `R` code:
  `dataHandle[[columnNameToWriteTo]] <- unlist(lapply(dataHandle[[columnNameToTakeFrom]], function(vi) { vi[[indexToTake]]}))`
but with all the steps happening on the Spark side (no data moving to/from `R`).

Note this could be solved by a solution to the following issue: https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/issues/649 .

title: consider providing commands to start spark cluster detached from session
description:
Feature request: Using sparklyr comamnds, be able to turn on/off an Spark cluster detached from the rsession.

Manual workaround follows:

```
./Users/<user>/Library/Caches/spark/spark-1.6.1-bin-hadoop2.6/sbin/start-master.sh 
```

http://localhost:8080/ contains to the master URL, for instance: `spark://<machine>:7077`.

```
./Users/<user>/Library/Caches/spark/spark-1.6.1-bin-hadoop2.6/sbin/start-slave.sh <master>
```

Then finally, to connect:

```
Sys.setenv(SPARK_HOME = "/Users/<user>/Library/Caches/spark/spark-1.6.1-bin-hadoop2.6/")

sc <- spark_connect(master = "spark://<machine>:7077")
```

Turn off cluster with:

```
./Users/<user>/Library/Caches/spark/spark-1.6.1-bin-hadoop2.6/sbin/stop-all.sh 
```

title: Feature request: sparklyr equivalent to SparkR::dapply
description:
If sparklyr had the equivalent or similar to `SparkR::dapply` then we could run R user defined functions on rows of data.  This would allow using package like `lubridate` at scale and build a very valuable "method of last resort" for solving `Spark` issues.

The function I want would have a signature like the following:

  `SparkR::dapply(dataHandle, Rfunction)`

The Rfunction source or closure (not sure which is more appropriate) would be shipped to the Spark cluster.  Spark would cut the data represented by dataHandle into reasonable sized contiguous row-intervals and call the Rfunction on each piece as an R data.frame.  The Rfunction must return a data.frame and then Spark would row-bind the pieces together in the same row-block order they were cut up.  This would allow the user to apply an arbitrary row transformation (such as `lubridate` parsing) very quickly.  This should be much cheaper than cutting up the data and sending it back to the controlling R instance as we are sending data to transient R instances on the cluster (as SparkR already does) and we thus also get parallelism.

I have an example of using the technique in SparkR here: https://github.com/WinVector/BigDataRStrata2017/blob/master/Exercises/solutions/06-Spark-Extension.md (please look for the `SparkR:dapply` section).

This is a huge capability that I think will greatly enhance Sparklyr.  It also means a lot of other issues (such as https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/issues/648 ) could be solved in terms of this operator.

title: Allow collection/persistence of ml_model objects
description:
I want to be able to reuse a model across connections.

Here's a linear regression of the [`cars`](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/datasets/topics/cars) dataset.

```r
library(dplyr)
library(sparklyr)

sc <- spark_connect("local")

# The classic cars dataset, plus some data to predict with
cars_tbl <- copy_to(sc, cars)
new_car_data <- data.frame(speed = seq(0, 100, 10))

# Any model will do; here's a linear regression
model <- cars_tbl %>% 
    ml_linear_regression("dist", "speed")
```

If I disconnect and reconnect, then making predictions no longer works.

```r
spark_disconnect(sc)
sc <- spark_connect("local")
new_car_data_tbl <- copy_to(sc, new_car_data)
model %>% predict(new_car_data_tbl)
## Error: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Object not found 139
```

I tried to persist the model using `sdf_persist()`, but that throws an error.

```r
sdf_persist(model)
## Error: Unable to retreive a Spark DataFrame from object of class ml_model_linear_regression ml_model
```

Some of the elements of the model are `spark_jobj`s, which (if I've understood them correctly) are connections to things in Spark. For example

```r
str(model$.model)
## Classes 'spark_jobj', 'shell_jobj' <environment: 0x1123e7120>
ls(model$.model)
## [1] "connection" "id"
```

I tried to collect the model to bring it into R, but no method has been implemented.

```r
collect(model)
## Error in UseMethod("collect") : 
##   no applicable method for 'collect' applied to an object of class "c('ml_model_linear_regression', 'ml_model')"
```

Due to the presence of these connection objects, saving the model using `saveRDS()` is also useless.

Have I missed some way to store an ml_model object? Or is it not currently possible?

library(nycflights13)

  c("year", "month", "day"), "carrier", "tailnum"))

yields

The equivalent `sparklyr` flavored operation:

title: Failure when JSON fields contain `\n` or `\r` characters
description:
Given the following json file:

```
path <- '/tmp/jsonissue.json'
cat('{"name":"Tim", "desc":"Multiline\\nText"}\n{"name":"Yates", "desc":"Single Text"}', file=path)
```

When we attempt to parse this with `sparklyr`:

```
library(sparklyr)
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", config = spark_config())
stock <- spark_read_json(sc, "stock", path)
head(stock)
spark_disconnect_all()
```

We get the following error:

```
Source:   query [2 x 2]
Database: spark connection master=local[4] app=sparklyr local=TRUE

Error: Variables must be length 1 or 3.
Problem variables: 'name' 
```

Running the same thing in SparkR gives the expected result:

```
library(SparkR)
sc <- sparkR.session(master = 'local')
stock <- read.json(path)
head(stock)
             desc  name
1 Multiline\nText   Tim
2     Single Text Yates
```

The problem is in the way sparklyr is parsing the `\\n` chars in the input json, as can be seen if we just go down to the single record in the json:

```
cat('{"name":"Tim", "desc":"Multiline\\nText"}', file=path)
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", config = spark_config())
stock <- spark_read_json(sc, "stock", path)
head(stock)
```

Which gives the result:

```
Source:   query [1 x 2]
Database: spark connection master=local[4] app=sparklyr local=TRUE

       desc  name
      <chr> <chr>
1 Multiline   Tim
2      Text   Tim
```

As you can see, the multiline field is applied across multiple records 😿

title: Long converted to numeric when using invoke_new()
description:
I need to pass a `long` Java object as a parameter to another constructor. However, since R has no long type, the Java long object is converted to a numeric. How can I go about this? Here is a reproducible example. 

```
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local")
long <- invoke_new(sc, "java.lang.Long", "100")

class(long)

invoke_new(sc = sc, "org.apache.spark.streaming.Duration", long)
```

I tried using the `rJava` function `.jlong` which supposedly creates a wrapper around the numeric so that it can be passed as a long parameter, but that does not work either.

```
library(rJava)
long <- .jlong(100)

class(long)
long

invoke_new(sc = sc, "org.apache.spark.streaming.Duration", long)
```

title: Altering captured reference damages spark results.
description:
If you use a variable in `dplyr::mutate()` against a `sparklyr` data source the lazy eval captures references to user variables.  Changing values of those variables implicitly changes the `mutate` and changes the values seen in the `sparklyr` result (which is itself a query).  This can be worked around by dropping in `dplyr::compute()` but it seems like it can produce a lot of incorrect calculations.  Below is a small example and a lot information on the versions of everything beeing run.  I am assuming the is a `sparklyr` issue as the query views are failrly different than a number of other `dplyr` structures, but it could be a `dplyr` issue.

title: Support for caching tables from other database apart from 'default' in Hive
description:
It's really a great package. I thank you all who are developing it. 
I'm pretty new with `sparklyr `  however I found following issues while trying to cache a table in Hive which is in different database than **default**.

Here is my code 
```
library(sparklyr)

sc <- spark_connect(master = "yarn-client", version="1.6.0", spark_home = '/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH/lib/spark/')

# works fine as airlines is in default database of Hive
tbl_cache(sc, 'airlines')

# this will not run [flat file DB]
# tbl_cache(sc, 'rbi_flat_file.ifsc_master')

# this also will not run [rbi DB is in ORC]
# tbl_cache(sc, 'rbi.ifsc_master')

# working
invoke(hive_context(sc), "sql", "USE rbi")
tbl_cache(sc, 'ifsc_master')
```
I got the solution from [this stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/33241105/caching-tables-in-spark-sql).

As a few idea [though I might be completely wrong]

1. I find that the function  `tbl_quote_name` in **R/tables_spark.R** is appending quote marks. Which may be modified to take . into account. 
2. Files **R/tables_spark.R** and **R/dplyr_spark_data.R** uses "CACHE TABLE" which may be modified if DB.TableName is given. 

Though the solution is not bad but a more general solution like use_db function in package will be helpful. Or at least it should be included in documentation like http://spark.rstudio.com/examples-cdh.html.

Another issue is with R-Studio interface is that when I ran last command in R-Studio entire list of tables under rbi DB become visible. While in Spark only two tables are cached.

title: ml_lda number of topics = columns of dataset why?
description:
When I look at the code of ml_lda, the number of topics is set to the number of columns from the dataset. Why would you do that as K is the number of topics you want to estimate, not the number of columns in the dataset.

```
model <- lda %>% invoke("setK", length(features)) %>% invoke("setFeaturesCol", 
        envir$features)
```

Wouldn't it make a lot more sense to provide the following types of arguments to ml_lda and use the setters accordingly?
- k = 5: number of topics
- optimizer = c("online", "em")
- alpha = docConcentration: Concentration parameter for the prior placed on documents' distributions over topics. If not missing, use setDocConcentration.
- beta = topicConcentration: for the prior placed on topics' distributions over terms. If not missing, use setTopicConcentration.
- maxIter = 100, 
- seed = 123456789
- subsamplingRate = 0.05

title: Would be more faithful to data if sparklyr represented NA as Spark lit(null:*) instead of blank and NaN.
description:
For Spark 2.0.0 spark-2.0.0-bin-hadoop2.7, sparklyr 0.4.26, dplyr 0.5.0, R 3.3.2, on OSX 10.11.6 I am seeing `NA` converted to blank (for strings/factors) and `NaN` for numeric when moving data from a local `data.frame` to `Spark`.  This seems needlessly unfaithful, as I think `Spark` has a NULL representation (please see [here](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/32067467/create-new-dataframe-with-empty-null-field-values) for some notes).  A complete example of the issue can be found [here](https://github.com/WinVector/replyr/blob/master/issues/NAvalues.md), and I am pasting the example below.

```
library('sparklyr')
packageVersion('sparklyr')
s200 <- my_db <- sparklyr::spark_connect(version='2.0.0', 
   master = "local")

d2 <- data.frame(x=factor(c('z1',NA,'z3')),y=c(3,5,NA),z=c(NA,'a','z'),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
print(d2)

d2r <- copy_to(s200,d2,'d2',
               temporary = FALSE,overwrite = TRUE)
print(d2r)
d2x <- as.data.frame(d2r)
print(d2x)
summary(d2x)
str(d2x)

    ## 'data.frame':    3 obs. of  3 variables:
    ##  $ x: chr  "z1" "" "z3"
    ##  $ y: num  3 5 NaN
    ##  $ z: chr  "" "a" "z"
```

title: dplyr / spark_read_csv() / High Column count Bug
description:
@javierluraschi @kevinushey 
Hey guys,

I ran into a bug using a combination of `dplyr` on a spark df that was created with `spark_read_csv()` that has more than 200 columns.  Since the built in `sdf_partition()` method has issues pertaining to large column counts ( issue #264 ) I'm attempting to work around this by appending a column to my dataset that contains a random number and then using that to partition the data.

There seems to be a bug that occurs when referencing the random number column which causes the rest of the data in the data frame to not be correctly reflected.  Below is a reproducible example.  What you'll see is that the v1 variable values (and all others if you look at the data) all change to 0 after partitioning based on the new random number column.  

```
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local")


# --------------------------------------------
# Simulate Dataset
# --------------------------------------------

df <- as.data.frame(matrix(0:1, ncol = 202, nrow = 100))
# sdf <- copy_to(sc, df, "df_test", overwrite = TRUE)

 
# export/import to CSV
file_name <- "C:\\Users\\pnieman\\Documents\\R\\lookaliketest\\data\\sdfrandtest.csv"
write.csv(x = df,file = file_name,row.names = FALSE)
sdf <- spark_read_csv(sc, "rt", path = file_name, overwrite = TRUE)


# Look at counts by v1 variable (You can see that v1 has both 1s and 0s)
sdf %>%
    group_by(v1) %>%
    summarise(ct = n())


# --------------------------------------------
# Partition Data
# --------------------------------------------

randtest <- sdf %>%
    mutate(rannum = rand()) %>%
    sdf_register("rt_diw")

# Partition based on Random Number 

partition_1 <- randtest %>%
    filter(rannum <= 0.8)

partition_2 <- randtest %>%
    filter(rannum > 0.8)


# Look at counts by "target" variable based on partitions (now everything are 0s!)
partition_1 %>%
    group_by(v1) %>%
    summarise(ct = n())

partition_2 %>%
    group_by(v1) %>%
    summarise(ct = n())
```


Other observations:

- This only occurs when there are more than 200 columns.  You can change this example to see.

- When using the `copy_to()` method instead of `spark_read_csv()` this seems to work as expected.  This code is included - just need to uncomment it out for testing and comment out the CSV section.  This leads me to believe that there may be some underlying issues with `spark_read_csv()`.

- The data in the `rt_diw` spark df looks correct, yet subsequent queries which use the rannum column result in bad data.

- No error is thrown in this... yet the data changes.  A little scary.

title: ml_tree_feature_importance
description:
It looks to me that the following code in ml_tree_feature_importance
`if (class(model)[1] != "ml_model_decision_tree") spark_require_version(sc, "2.0.0")`
should be replaced with
`if (class(model)[1] %in% c("ml_model_decision_tree", "ml_model_gradient_boosted_trees")) spark_require_version(sc, "2.0.0")`

As it is only org.apache.spark.ml.regression.DecisionTreeRegressor and org.apache.spark.ml.regression.GBTRegressionModel which do not have a featureImportances method in Spark 1.6, while org.apache.spark.ml.regression.RandomForestRegressionModel already has this in Spark 1.6

The following gives errors for that reason.

```
library(PASWR)
library(sparklyr)
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", version = "1.6.2", hadoop_version = "2.6")

data(titanic3, package = "PASWR")
x <- titanic3[, c("name", "pclass", "survived", "fare", "age", "sex")]
x <- na.exclude(x)
x <- copy_to(dest = sc, df = x, 
             name = "titanic3", overwrite = TRUE)

## Fit regression tree
m <- ml_decision_tree(x, response = fare ~ survived + age + sex, 
                      max.bins = 32, max.depth = 5,
                      type = "regression")
ml_tree_feature_importance(sc, m)
Error: failed to invoke spark command (unknown reason)
```

title: drat repository for sparklyr
description: Sparklyr is pretty actively developed, and AFAIK you are pushing to master, which potentially makes a risk of sparklyr to be in a state in which it won't pass unit tests. I would like to plug sparklyr devel into my CI pipeline, but it could be painful to depend on a devel package which might not pass own tests. Ideally would be if you could setup drat repository which would be updated only when unit tests passed fine. Then any downstream packages that imports sparklyr wouldn't be affected by a temporary issues that may always appear in master.

title: Performance difference between Spark and Sparklyr
description:
Good Afternoon all -

This is NOT an issue but a question to understand how Sparklyr works.

SCENARIO:
Take the MNIST data from https://www.kaggle.com/c/digit-recognizer/data. Run PCA on the training data to reduce the dimension of the dataset to 150 features. Using PrComp from R is fine for it. Reformulate the data to have the label and the 150 PCs (Principal Components) as a new data file. In order to test and validate split the data in training set and test set (29K and 13K respectively) 

TEST:

On the above formed new dataset, run neural network with 150 input nodes, 5 nodes in the hidden layer, 10 output nodes using Spark REPL and Sparklyr. Additional features to be set: seed = 1234L, max iterations = 100

RESULTS:

Spark's REPL (Scala) takes 427 seconds to execute.
Sparklyr takes only 141 seconds to execute.

The results are same 67.2% accuracy. 

QUESTION:

How is it possible for Sparklyr to finish the job in that short amount of time when compared to Scala code? The code that I have written on both Spark and Sparklyr is similar:
1. Initialize the Neural Network with the appropriate options such as seed, layers and max iteration
2. Fit the training data
3. Transform the test data.

Other computations such as evaluation of the classifier and computation of accuracy and error in not part of the benchmark time.

Please let me know your thoughts on this matter.

Sincerely
Lalit Nookala

title: implement save / load for 'ml_model' objects
description:
The tricky part in saving these is that we also need a bit of extra metadata to re-construct the R object wrapper housing the Spark model object. So, on save, we would likely need to write two files, e.g.

```
/path/to/model_fit.mldata
/path/to/model_fit.rdata
```

The `model_fit.mldata` object would be created by e.g. `invoke(model$.model, "save", "/path/to/model_fit.mldata")`; the `model_fit.rdata` object might be implemented by e.g. `saveRDS()` and then copying that file to the Spark filesystem.

Loading would then just re-construct the `ml_model` object by loading the two files and duct-taping them back together.

title: 'collect()' sometimes produces wrong result from 'copy_to()'ed datasets
description:
Repro -- the following program fails:

```
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)

sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", version = "2.0.0")

n <- 1E3
df <- as.data.frame(replicate(n, 1L, FALSE))
names(df) <- paste("X", 1:n, sep = "")

options(sparklyr.collect.chunk.size = 2^31 - 1)
tbl <- copy_to(sc, df, overwrite = TRUE)
cl <- as.data.frame(collect(tbl))
stopifnot(identical(df, cl))
```

Yet, the following works fine:

```
# OK
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)

sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", version = "2.0.0")

n <- 1E3
df <- as.data.frame(replicate(n, 1L, FALSE))
names(df) <- paste("X", 1:n, sep = "")

path <- tempfile()
write.table(df, file = path, row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE, sep = ",", quote = FALSE)

options(sparklyr.collect.chunk.size = 2^31 - 1)
tbl <- spark_session(sc) %>%
  invoke("read") %>%
  invoke("format", "com.databricks.spark.csv") %>%
  invoke("option", "header", TRUE) %>%
  invoke("option", "inferSchema", TRUE) %>%
  invoke("load", path) %>%
  sdf_register()

cl <- as.data.frame(collect(tbl))
stopifnot(identical(cl, df))
```

So we must be doing something strange in our implementation of `copy_to()` that infects how `collect()` operates. @javierluraschi, do you have any ideas?

title: pmin and pmax are unsupported
description:
Using pmin or pmax to get the elementwise minima or maxima of two columns does not work with a Spark backend. The following code works when using a plain R backend (and I believe most databases too).

`df_test <- data.frame(x=c(1, 2, 3), y=c(2, 1, 2))
df_test %>% mutate(pmin(x,y))`

However, the following code with the same data in Spark does not.

`sc = spark_connect(master='local')
copy_to(sc, df_test)
sdf_load_table(sc, 'df_test') %>% mutate(pmin(x,y)) 
`

The error comes from Spark itself in Scala. The first line of the stack trace is
`Error: org.apache.spark.sql.AnalysisException: Invalid number of arguments for function min; line 2 pos 23`

With the help of some wiser Spark folks, I see that the min and max functions in Spark expect only one argument. Since the SQL generated by pmin and pmax uses MIN and MAX, I'm not sure where the fix should occur. Thanks for any help.

varnumeric <- c("DepTime","Distance")
featvars <- c(varchars,varnumeric)

```
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_CONF_DIR="/etc/hadoop/conf")

### My changed `ml_kmeans` function is below

``` R
ml_kmeans <- function(x,
                      centers,
                      max.iter = 100,
                      features = dplyr::tbl_vars(x),
                      compute.cost = TRUE,
                      epsilon = 0.0001,
                      mode = "k-means||",
                      ...) {

  df <- spark_dataframe(x)
  sc <- spark_connection(df)

  df <- ml_prepare_features(df, features)

  centers <- ensure_scalar_integer(centers)
  max.iter <- ensure_scalar_integer(max.iter)
  only_model <- ensure_scalar_boolean(list(...)$only_model, default = FALSE)
  epsilon <- ensure_scalar_double(epsilon)

  assert_that(mode %in% c("random", "k-means||"))
  mode <- ensure_scalar_character(mode)

  envir <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())

  envir$id <- sparklyr:::random_string("id_")
  df <- df %>%
    sdf_with_unique_id(envir$id) %>%
    spark_dataframe()

  tdf <- ml_prepare_dataframe(df, features, envir = envir)

  envir$model <- "org.apache.spark.ml.clustering.KMeans"
  kmeans <- invoke_new(sc, envir$model)

  model <- kmeans %>%
    invoke("setK", centers) %>%
    invoke("setMaxIter", max.iter) %>%
    invoke("setEpsilon", epsilon) %>%
    invoke("setInitializationMode", mode) %>%
    invoke("setFeaturesCol", envir$features) %>%


  if (only_model) return(model)

  fit <- model %>%
    invoke("fit", tdf)

  # extract cluster centers
  kmmCenters <- invoke(fit, "clusterCenters")

  # compute cost for k-means
  if (compute.cost)
    kmmCost <- invoke(fit, "computeCost", tdf)

  centersList <- transpose_list(lapply(kmmCenters, function(center) {
    as.numeric(invoke(center, "toArray"))
  }))

  names(centersList) <- features
  centers <- as.data.frame(centersList, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, optional = TRUE)

  ml_model("kmeans", fit,
           centers = centers,
           features = features,
           data = df,
           model.parameters = as.list(envir),
           cost = ifelse(compute.cost, kmmCost, NULL)
  )
}
```

title: handle model predictions with categorical variables
description:
E.g.

```
> library(sparklyr)
> library(dplyr)
> sc <- spark_connect(master = "local")
> train <- iris
> valid <- iris[-c(1:50), ]
> iris_train <- copy_to(sc, train, overwrite = T)
> iris_valid <- copy_to(sc, valid, overwrite = T)
> ml1 <- ml_linear_regression(iris_train, Sepal_Length ~ Species)
> sdf_predict(ml1, iris_valid)
Error: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Field "Speciesversicolor" does not exist.
    at org.apache.spark.sql.types.StructType$$anonfun$apply$1.apply(StructType.scala:212)
    at org.apache.spark.sql.types.StructType$$anonfun$apply$1.apply(StructType.scala:212)
    at scala.collection.MapLike$class.getOrElse(MapLike.scala:128)
    at scala.collection.AbstractMap.getOrElse(Map.scala:58)
    at org.apache.spark.sql.types.StructType.apply(StructType.scala:211)
    at org.apache.spark.ml.feature.VectorAssembler$$anonfun$2.apply(VectorAssembler.scala:55)
    at org.apache.spark.ml.feature.VectorAssembler$$anonfun$2.apply(VectorAssembler.scala:54)
    at scala.collection.TraversableLike$$anonfun$flatMap$1.apply(TraversableLike.scala:251)
    at scala.collection.TraversableLike$$anonfun$flatMap$1.apply(TraversableLike.scala:251)

The problem here is that, because `versicolor` is not detected as a level in the prediction data set, a dummy variable is not created for it on the fly and prediction fails. We should save the detected levels from the original dataset and use that when constructing dummy variables.

title: Survival Regression
description:
Guys, could add to the ML outputs for Survival Regression the scale? 

In the code below should be added something like:

```
scale = invoke(fit, "scale")
```

This should be linked with the model coefficients of this ML model. 

```
ml_survival_regression
function (x, response, features, intercept = TRUE, censor = "censor", 
    max.iter = 100L, ...) 
{
    df <- spark_dataframe(x)
    sc <- spark_connection(df)
    df <- ml_prepare_response_features_intercept(df, response, 
        features, intercept)
    censor <- ensure_scalar_character(censor)
    max.iter <- ensure_scalar_integer(max.iter)
    only_model <- ensure_scalar_boolean(list(...)$only_model, 
        default = FALSE)
    envir <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    tdf <- ml_prepare_dataframe(df, features, response, envir = envir)
    model <- "org.apache.spark.ml.regression.AFTSurvivalRegression"
    rf <- invoke_new(sc, model)
    model <- rf %>% invoke("setMaxIter", max.iter) %>% invoke("setFeaturesCol", 
        envir$features) %>% invoke("setLabelCol", envir$response) %>% 
        invoke("setFitIntercept", as.logical(intercept)) %>% 
        invoke("setCensorCol", censor)
    if (only_model) 
        return(model)
    fit <- model %>% invoke("fit", tdf)
    coefficients <- fit %>% invoke("coefficients") %>% invoke("toArray")
    names(coefficients) <- features
    hasIntercept <- invoke(fit, "getFitIntercept")
    if (hasIntercept) {
        intercept <- invoke(fit, "intercept")
        coefficients <- c(coefficients, intercept)
        names(coefficients) <- c(features, "(Intercept)")
    }
    coefficients <- intercept_first(coefficients)
    ml_model("survival_regression", fit, features = features, 
        response = response, intercept = intercept, coefficients = coefficients, 
        intercept = intercept, model.parameters = as.list(envir))
}
<environment: namespace:sparklyr>
```

Thanks,
Eliano

title: placing predicted values into spark dataframes
description:
As a normal R user, I am used to running a pattern like this. 

```
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local")
iris_tbl <- copy_to(sc, iris)

mod <- iris_tbl %>% 
  ml_random_forest(
    response = "Species", 
    features = c("Sepal_Length", "Sepal_Width",  "Petal_Length", "Petal_Width")
  )

pred <- predict(mod, newdata = iris_tbl)

iris_tbl %>% 
  mutate(pred = predict(mod, newdata = iris_tbl)) %>% 
  collect
```

This seems to not work as the `predict` function returns values back into R-land, not into spark-land. In this case you'll get an error because `sparklyr` is trying to translate the predict statement into sql. 

```
Error in UseMethod("escape") : 
  no applicable method for 'escape' applied to an object of class "c('ml_model_random_forest', 'ml_model')"
In addition: Warning message:
Named arguments ignored for SQL PREDICT 
```

In this case it's not such a terrible thing because the iris dataset is nice and small and the [tutorial](http://spark.rstudio.com/mllib.html#linear_regression) deals with this situation by first bringing all the data back into Rland. But if the dataset was very big then I would prefer the confusion matrix to be calculated on the spark side. 

Is there a way to get predicted values back into the spark-dataframe? The usecase would be to check performance in a training set and run some custom metrics against it. Spark tends to have it's [own metrics](http://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/mllib-evaluation-metrics.html) which potentially could offer an alternative here as well but I have not seen that supported in the docs.

title: How to enable mode overwrite or append in spark_write_parquet() function?
description:
Dear @javierluraschi,  would you mind adding support for options such as overwrite or append in spark_write_parquet() function?

On the other hand, spark_read_parquet() allows users controlling for mergeSchema = "true" or mergeSchema = "false"? I think it is an important option due to schema evolution in many data bases along time, starting with a simple schema, and gradually adding more columns to the schema as needed. The function loadDF in SparkR package allows users set the option mergeSchema, keeping it false by default. http://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sql-programming-guide.html#schema-merging

Thanks.

title: consider refactoring 'spark_api' family of functions
description:
It's often not clear to me what a particular `spark_api_*` function does; in particular, it always takes me a few minutes to figure out what the function accepts, and what the function returns, when I can use it, etc.

The word `api` in this context is not particularly evocative, so I hope we can choose more informative names. For functions that return a (static) `jobj` attached to `sc` or its associated `sconInst`, I think these functions should also (only?) accept the plain `sparklyr_connection` object if possible.

title: `collect()` fails when one column returns to R as a jobj
description:
Repro:

```
library(rspark)
library(dplyr)

sc <- spark_connect("local", version = "1.6.1")

data(diamonds)
diamonds_tbl <- copy_to(sc, diamonds, "diamonds")

diamonds_tbl %>%
  sdf_mutate(assembled = ft_vector_assembler(c("x", "y", "z")))
```

Prints the error:

```
> diamonds_tbl %>%
+   ml_mutate(assembled = ft_vector_assembler(c("x", "y", "z")))
Source:   query [?? x 11]
Database: spark connection master=local app=rspark local=TRUE

 Show Traceback

 Rerun with Debug
 Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE) : 
  cannot coerce class ""jobj"" to a data.frame 
```

This occurs because the newly-created `assembled` column is actually a `list-of-lists` column, which apparently gets serialized as a `jobj`. We should see if we can read this back as a list-of-lists.

title: ClassCastException using copy_to with "flights" data in cluster mode
description:
- Connect to Spark cluster on EC2
- Run:

```
flights_tbl <- copy_to(sc, flights, "flights", overwrite = TRUE)
```

This takes a long time, and eventually comes back with this error:

```
Error: org.apache.spark.SparkException: Job aborted due to stage failure: Task 0 in stage 2.0 failed 4 times, most recent failure: Lost task 0.3 in stage 2.0 (TID 7, ip-10-231-88-23.ec2.internal): java.lang.ClassCastException: java.sql.Timestamp cannot be cast to java.lang.Double
```
- The error is caused by the last column of `flights` (`time_hour`). Try `copy_to` the `flights` data without that column:

```
flights_sub <- select(flights, year:minute)
flights_tbl <- copy_to(sc, flights_sub, "flights_sub", overwrite = TRUE)
```

This works fine (still takes long; about 9 minutes)

title: add support for running on windows
description:
Currently running on Windows is possible but impractical due to the requirements associated with setting file permissions for Hive (it requires download of cygwin utilities and their required MSVC runtime DLLs then executing some commands within the Windows console). See this PR for details: https://github.com/rstudio/sparklyr/pull/39

In order to head off the confusion and hemorrhaging of time which will ensue if users try to get all this working we're going to temporarily disable support for Windows and provide a link to this issue so that users can be notified when we have a better solution (hopefully very soon!).

Note that users who wish to plow ahead and try to get things working on Windows can set the following option to re-enable Windows support:

``` r
options(sparklyr.windows_enabled = TRUE)
```

This option should be enabled within `.Rprofile` so that it is set at the beginning of every R session.

Executing the `spark_install` function will then print the additional instructions for running on Windows:

``` r
library(sparklyr)
spark_install(version = "1.6.1")
```

title: spark_apply() with the default packages = TRUE fails when the executor's user doesn't own its working directory
description:
## Problem

With the default `packages = TRUE`, `spark_apply()` fails on every task when the executor runs under a uid that can write to its working directory but doesn't own it:

```
org.apache.spark.SparkException: Process List(tar, -xf, packages.24638.tar) exited with code 2
```

The executor log shows why:

```
INFO Utils: Untarring packages.93312.tar
INFO Utils: tar: .: Cannot utime: Operation not permitted
INFO Utils: tar: .: Cannot change mode to rwxr-xr-t: Operation not permitted
INFO Utils: tar: Exiting with failure status due to previous errors
ERROR Utils: Process List(tar, -xf, packages.93312.tar) exited with code 2:
```

Spark supports this setup. The Kubernetes Dockerfile in the Spark distribution (`kubernetes/dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile`, 3.5.9 and 4.2.0) leaves `/opt/spark/work-dir` owned by root, makes it group-writable (`chmod g+w`), and runs as `USER 185` with no account. Its entrypoint adds a passwd entry for whatever uid the container gets. It is meant for platforms that assign arbitrary uids, such as OpenShift. The official `apache/spark` images `chown` the directory to their `spark` user, so they don't show the problem.

We hit it on Kubernetes with executors that run as each user's own uid (`securityContext.runAsUser`, `runAsNonRoot`) and a root-owned, world-writable `/opt/spark/work-dir` (mode 1777).

## Cause

`spark_apply_bundle()` archives each library path with a `.` entry (`R/spark_apply.R`, lines 787–791 on main at 2249e85):

```r
args <- c("-chf", packagesTar, if (isTRUE(packages)) {
  lapply(.libPaths(), function(e) {
    c("-C", e, ".")
  }) ...
```

The bundle goes through `SparkContext.addFile()`, so Spark runs `tar -xf` in the executor's working directory. GNU tar then tries to set that directory's timestamp and mode from the archive's `.` entry. Only the directory's owner may do that, so tar exits with status 2. (Spark also logs that untarring via `addFile` will be deprecated in favour of `spark.archives`.)

The named-package path works on the same cluster. `spark_apply(f, packages = c("dplyr"))` archives `-C <lib> dplyr rlang ...`, which has no `.` entry, and it succeeds.

## Reproduction (no Spark needed)

```sh
docker run --rm ubuntu:26.04 bash -c 'mkdir -m 1777 /work && su -s /bin/bash nobody -c "
  mkdir -p /tmp/lib/pkgA && echo x > /tmp/lib/pkgA/f
  tar -cf /tmp/dot.tar -C /tmp/lib . && tar -cf /tmp/named.tar -C /tmp/lib pkgA
  cd /work && tar -xf /tmp/dot.tar; echo dot-exit=\$?
  rm -rf /work/pkgA; tar -xf /tmp/named.tar; echo named-exit=\$?"'
```

```
tar: .: Cannot utime: Operation not permitted
tar: .: Cannot change mode to rwxr-xr-t: Operation not permitted
tar: Exiting with failure status due to previous errors

## Suggested fix

Archive each library's entries by name instead of `.`, for example:

```r
lapply(.libPaths(), function(e) {
  entries <- list.files(e, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE)
  if (length(entries) > 0) c("-C", e, entries) else NULL
})
```

The bundle's contents stay the same, and it unpacks wherever the executor can write.
